articles.title: Incomplete remedies: On Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The ECI offers relief to a section of deleted electors but SIR’s flaws remain

Following the Special Summary Revision (SSR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI) in some States that had undergone the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) , mostly in Phases 1 and 2, some 74 lakh names were added onto the electoral rolls. This meant that the electorate in those 13 States, that had shrunk from 49.61 crore to 45.22 crore after the SIR, has now gone up to 45.96 crore. The ECI has extended the SSR to States and UTs in Phase 3. As before, it requires no proof of citizenship or mapping to older rolls, and insists on personal notice before any deletion other than of the dead. It also directs Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to cross-verify deletions personally wherever they exceed 2% of a polling station’s electors. Draft deletions in Phase 3 of the SIR averaged 17% , and reached 32.8% in Delhi . The ECI also offered another opportunity to electors deleted by the SIR in the seven States and UTs where it is still underway, such as Delhi and Maharashtra, to return to the rolls. Electors who did not return their forms can do so now, explaining the delay, and those who moved within the State can return through the enumeration form with proof of their new address. EROs will process these forms under Rule 21(1) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and restore the elector’s old EPIC number.

These “corrective” measures follow the Supreme Court’s observation on October 28 that forcing deleted electors to re-enrol through Form 6, meant for new voters, was an “error”. The ECI’s use of remedies that existed in the registration rules is a tacit admission that it went wrong during the SIR. But the measures are limited. They reach roughly 4.5 crore of the 13.37 crore struck off the draft rolls and do not cover electors who moved out of their States. Electors in States where the SIR has concluded, including Bihar and West Bengal, which have already voted on the SIR rolls, can return only through the SSR, by filing Form 6 as new voters, with fresh EPIC numbers and no record that they were ever on the roll. In essence, the structure of the SIR remains intact. Electors must still provide details from “the last SIR”, and those whose details are unavailable or do not match will be asked for documents in a manner that amounts to a citizenship test. The legality of the ludicrous “logical discrepancy” checks remains unaddressed. The 2002-03 special revision offered a better way. Those who had shifted homes were enumerated door to door at their new addresses. The Supreme Court must direct the ECI to return to that model.

The ECI’s use of remedies that existed in the registration rules is a tacit admission that it went wrong during the SIR. But the measures are limited. They reach roughly 4.5 crore of the 13.37 crore struck off the draft rolls and do not cover electors who moved out of their States. Electors in States where the SIR has concluded, including Bihar and West Bengal, which have already voted on the SIR rolls, can return only through the SSR, by filing Form 6 as new voters, with fresh EPIC numbers and no record that they were ever on the roll. In essence, the structure of the SIR remains intact. Electors must still provide details from “the last SIR”, and those whose details are unavailable or do not match will be asked for documents in a manner that amounts to a citizenship test. The legality of the ludicrous “logical discrepancy” checks remains unaddressed. The 2002-03 special revision offered a better way. Those who had shifted homes were enumerated door to door at their new addresses. The Supreme Court must direct the ECI to return to that model.

fullParagraphs: Europe must be part of any settlement on the Ukraine war

The trilateral negotiations in Abu Dhabi between Russia, Ukraine and the U.S. earlier this month failed to produce a major breakthrough or bridge the wide gap between Kyiv and Moscow. Yet, they were a good beginning towards finding a political settlement to Europe’s longest war since the Second World War . In the two-day talks, hosted by the U.S., the warring sides agreed on some humanitarian measures, including prisoner exchange. U.S. representatives Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow after the talks to discuss the proposal. In the next stage, U.S., Ukrainian and European officials will meet in Berlin to discuss a coordinated European and Ukrainian position towards the peace process. As of now, Russian and Ukrainian positions remain far apart. Russia demands Ukraine withdraw from the territories of Donbas it still controls to stop attacks. Russia also wants to introduce limits to Ukrainian military capabilities and Kyiv to declare neutrality (give up its NATO ambitions). Ukraine, on the other hand, has rejected making any territorial concessions for a settlement and asked for security guarantees from the West so that Russia would not attack the country again.

That Ukraine survived Russia’s invasion and continued to resist Russian forces for almost five years is no small feat. But it has also paid a huge price for its resistance. The country has lost more than 20% of its territory. Millions have fled, while men of fighting age are being drafted into the military . Ukraine’s economy is kept afloat by European support, while its military continues to rely on NATO for weapons and other supplies. Until recently, the West stood united in its support for Ukraine against Russia, but that unity has since begun to fray. U.S. President Donald Trump, who has lifted sanctions on Russian diesel, is seeking to reset Washington’s ties with Moscow . European leaders, who initially sought to isolate Russia, have also started reestablishing contacts with the Kremlin. In October, Finnish and Norwegian leaders held direct talks with Mr. Putin. To be sure, Ukraine’s long-range strikes can hurt Russia, as the recent attack on the Kerch Bridge demonstrated. But such strikes are unlikely to change the Kremlin’s thinking about the war. As the conflict drags on, Ukraine’s position is weakening, and its allies are growing increasingly divided. After almost five years, Russia has failed to take a decisive victory. Ukraine does not have a credible path towards victory either. A diplomatic settlement, therefore, is the only way forward. The Abu Dhabi talks recognised this reality. But for the process to be meaningful, Europe must also be brought to the negotiating table.

fullParagraphs: A 42-year-old man sustained minor injuries on his left thigh after being bitten by a crocodile that strayed into a house in Koppadi village near Chidambaram on Sunday.

According to police sources, P. Ilavarasan of Koppadi village was staying in his house when a dog began to bark continuously. When he went outside he was shocked to see a crocodile. The reptile lunged at him and attacked Ilavarasan on his left thigh. Hearing his cries, neighbours rushed to the spot and alerted the Forest Department.
Forest Department personnel arrived and, with the help of residents, safely captured the crocodile and released it into the Vakkaramari lake in Chidambaram.

articles.title: Pattabiram residents urge Highways dept. to build roundabouton CTH Road junction
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Residents of Pattabiram have urged the Highways Department to build a roundabout on the Chennai–Tiruvallur High Road (CTH) or Chennai–Tirupati–Renigunta Road near the flyover, replacing the Level Crossing 2 on the railway siding.
Without a roundabout, the six-way junction presents a chaotic sight during peak hours, said Roy Rozario, a resident.
Apart from the lanes of the C.T.H Road, road to/from Poonamallee and M.G. Road join the junction. People heading to the police station, TIDEL Park, hotels, schools, and colleges use the junction.

“Due to the lack of a roundabout, a lot of accidents happen as people drive on the wrong side of the road or drive recklessly. Long ago, the government had announced that a roundabout would be constructedat the location. We hope that it would come up soon,” he added.

Residents, meanwhile, have urged the department to open the other side of the flyover to traffic. “It has been completed. Only some works such as lighting, removal of excess cement concrete, and painting seem to remain. Though the surface is rough, people are driving on the incomplete side of the flyover to reach the other side,” said T. Sadagopan, activist.
The space beneath the flyover must also be cleared and the roads must be laid properly.

“Several bus services from Poonamallee, Thiruninravur, and other places have been cut, as there is no space to park the buses. Those buses that start from Pattabiram wait at random spots on the C.T.H Road. We want the Highways to also construct a foot overbridge beneath the flyover, or a limited-use subway,” said a resident.
Sources said the roundabout would be formed during the widening of the road. As far as a subway or a foot overbridge was concerned, necessary studies would be taken up.

articles.title: Six sent to juvenile home after Mumbai assault; Maharashtra SP leader seeks age change
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Police registered a case and produced all eight before the Board, and notices were sent to parents; the case was registered under sections 189(2), 189(4), 118(1), 352 and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, says Deputy Commissioner of Police

A juvenile court in Mumbai on Saturday sent six minors to a juvenile correctional home till December 4 in connection with the alleged assault of a couple at a garden in Kurla on Friday evening, police said on Sunday. The six are aged between 12 and 15, the Ghatkopar police said.

Deputy Commissioner of Police Ganesh Shinde said an FIR was lodged against the minors under Sections 189(2) (unlawful assembly), 118(1) (voluntarily causing hurt using dangerous weapons or means), 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace), and 351(2) (criminal intimidation) and other relevant provisions of the BNS.
All of them were produced before the Juvenile Justice Board and notices were sent to their parents.

According to the police, the couple was at the garden behind Phoenix Marketcity mall when a group of minors surrounded them and began to abuse them. When the couple tried to reason with the group, they assaulted them with a hockey stick and forced them out of the garden. Police detained them after a video of the incident surfaced on social media.
The police said they are recording the statements of the couple and the juveniles to determine whether the two groups had a dispute before the incident that took place at the Pramod Mahajan Garden.

The incident drew sharp reactions from political parties, with many condemning it. Samajwadi Party Maharashtra president Abu Asim Azmi said the juvenile age threshold should be brought down from 18 to 15 and that those below 18 years who commit murder, robbery or harassment should not be given concessions under the law. Mr. Azmi added that the incident should not be linked to religion and that the law should act without discrimination.
Meanwhile, BJP leader Kirit Somaiya met the couple at the Ghatkopar police station and promised action.

NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule urged Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, who holds the Home portfolio, to “adopt a no-tolerance policy towards such incidents” and said citizens should be able to move around freely in the State.
Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Intekhab Farooqui also condemned the assault.

articles.title: Over 40% Group A posts vacant at PGIMS Rohtak, says former Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Alleging that 41.6% of the sanctioned Group A posts at the Post-Graduate Institute of Medical Sciences (PGIMS) in Rohtak were lying vacant, former Haryana Home Minister Subhash Batra on Sunday questioned the BJP government’s claims of improving healthcare services in the State.

Citing an inspection by the Assembly’s Subject Committee in February, Mr. Batra said 424 of the 1,018 sanctioned Group A posts at the institute were vacant. He said the shortage of doctors, specialists and healthcare staff was affecting patient care at the institute, which catered to over 8,000 patients daily in its outpatient department.
Manjunath, in-charge of the Public Relations Department, PGIMS, did not respond to repeated calls and messages seeking his response to the former Minister’s allegations.

Addressing a press conference, Mr. Batra also pointed out that only 200 of the 540 medicines on the government-approved list were available in the hospital store during the Health Minister’s inspection in April. Supply orders for 172 types of medicines and surgical materials were pending with companies, he alleged.

Alleging that the “condition of the Radiology Department is also extremely concerning”, Mr. Batra said 10 of the 13 sanctioned faculty posts and nine of the 11 Senior Resident posts were vacant in the department, as per a September-October 2026 report. Of the nearly 500 patients advised ultrasound examinations daily, only 40% could undergo the test on the same day, he added.

Questioning the gap between budgetary allocations and the availability of health care facilities, Mr. Batra said ₹1,232 crore had been allocated to the Pandit Bhagwat Dayal Sharma University of Health Sciences and PGIMS for 2026-27, an increase of ₹422 crore over the previous year, but patients continued to face shortages of medicines and delays in diagnostic tests.
Mr. Batra also raised concerns over two incidents of ceiling plaster falling in the old hospital building in October.

On behalf of the Congress, Mr. Batra demanded that all vacant posts be filled, medicine stocks and pending complaints be made public, diagnostic facilities expanded and old hospital buildings subjected to a safety audit.

“The poor, labourers, farmers and the middle-class families in the State need doctors on time, essential medicines and quality treatment and not speeches and announcements,” he said, adding that the Congress would continue to raise this serious issue concerning health and hold the government accountable.

In the teachers quiz competition, Savitha and Sreeja of Sunbeam CBSE School. Muthanara. and Anushya - Spark School, Savitha and Monisha of Shrishti Vidyashram School won first, second and third prizes respectively, the release said.

articles.title: Coal auction rounds attract 85 bids; 20 first-time players enter sector
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The 16th round of commercial mine auctions put forth 25 blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines.
The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions has attracted 83 bids for 17 coal blocks with 20 first-time bidders seeking to enter commercial coal mining, signalling fresh interest in the sector.
The Union Coal Ministry said on Friday that 17 blocks offered in the latest round received 83 bids. In addition, the second attempt to auction one coal block from the 15th round attracted two bids.
Taking the 26 blocks covered by the auction process into account, the number of bids has quadrupled compared with the previous round, the ministry said.
The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions was launched on September 17, offering 25 blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines.

“Competition in the current round has been intense, with 16 of the 26 blocks attracting multiple bids. The round has also brought 20 first-time bidders into the commercial coal mining regime, a clear sign that the sector continues to draw new capital and new players,” the ministry said in a statement.

Since the introduction of the commercial coal mining auction regime in June 2020, the government has auctioned 145 coal mines across 15 rounds. These mines are estimated to generate annual revenues of around ₹47,500 crore, according to government estimates.

The 16th round of commercial mine auctions put forth 25 blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines.

The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions has attracted 83 bids for 17 coal blocks with 20 first-time bidders seeking to enter commercial coal mining, signalling fresh interest in the sector.

The Union Coal Ministry said on Friday that 17 blocks offered in the latest round received 83 bids. In addition, the second attempt to auction one coal block from the 15th round attracted two bids.

Taking the 26 blocks covered by the auction process into account, the number of bids has quadrupled compared with the previous round, the ministry said.

The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions was launched on September 17, offering 25 blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines.

“Competition in the current round has been intense, with 16 of the 26 blocks attracting multiple bids. The round has also brought 20 first-time bidders into the commercial coal mining regime, a clear sign that the sector continues to draw new capital and new players,” the ministry said in a statement.

Since the introduction of the commercial coal mining auction regime in June 2020, the government has auctioned 145 coal mines across 15 rounds. These mines are estimated to generate annual revenues of around ₹47,500 crore, according to government estimates.

articles.title: Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties end talks without deal on forming Israel government
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: ‘The latest round of coalition talks... has concluded; the two sides outlined their positions on a range of substantive issues and discussed them in detail,’ the two parties said in a joint statement

The parties of caretaker Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot concluded a new round of talks on Sunday (November 22, 2026) without reaching an agreement on a possible coalition government, which would require concessions from both sides.
Delegations from Eisenkot's Yashar party and Netanyahu's Likud met for four hours at a hotel in Herzliya, near Tel Aviv, following a first round of discussions last Sunday (November 22).

"The latest round of coalition talks... has concluded. The two sides outlined their positions on a range of substantive issues and discussed them in detail," the two parties said in a joint statement.
"A follow-up meeting will be held," they added, without specifying a date or revealing any other details.
A former army chief of staff, Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government, with the possibility of a 14?day extension, after October elections failed to give either camp an absolute majority.

His 48-member bloc, which needs 61 lawmakers to reach a majority, remains divided over whether to build a coalition through an alliance with ultra?Orthodox parties, a rapprochement with Arab parties, or a national unity government with Likud.
Netanyahu is pushing for a national unity government, which could see a rotation of the premiership between the two men, a mechanism already tried in Israel.

Such an arrangement could allow Netanyahu to keep his political protection against the corruption charges he faces, as well as continue to oppose the creation of an independent commission of inquiry into the security failures that preceded the Hamas attack of October 7, 2023.
But that prospect runs up against Eisenkot's refusal to serve in a cabinet led by Netanyahu, against whom he centred his campaign.
His ally Naftali Bennett, a former prime minister, also reiterated on Saturday his refusal to join a coalition with "Netanyahu or his bloc, under any circumstances".

articles.title: COP31 talks fail as EU, others reject any climate deal without language on a fossil fuel phase-out
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: EU, Panama among about 130 parties that refuse to accept COP President’s consensus cover text, alleges that it “greenwashes” fossil fuels; India, China, Saudi Arabia are on the other side of the divide

A standoff on a fossil fuel phase-out prevented countries at COP 31, the United Nations climate talks in Antalya, Turkiye, from achieving any consensus agreement on future climate action on Sunday (November 22, 2026), despite the conference running a record 48 hours into overtime.

The European Union led objections to COP 31 President Murat Kurum’s consensus cover text that failed to include any explicit language about moving away from fossil fuels. The EU’s stance was reportedly supported by about 130 countries.

On the other side of the divide, India is among the nations that supported the proposed cover text, as they want to keep using fossil fuels for the foreseeable future, with Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav stressing that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation.”

“We express profound disappointment with the final draft COP31 cover decision or Antalya Pact. At a point where the world urgently needs action to avert disastrous levels of global warming, the draft cover decision falls well short,” Ireland’s Climate Minister Darragh O’Brien said, speaking on behalf of the EU.

“We will not endorse a decision that does not respond to the science, that disregards the implementation gap, and that actually risks deepening the chasm between global commitments and the action required to correct the overshoot and bring 1.5 degrees back to within reach… We will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel,” he added.

A cover text is an overarching political decision that frames the outcome of a climate conference rather than settling any single agenda item. It is usually finalised last, and like every outcome, it needs the consensus of all parties.

Panama also formally objected to the text, saying that as a country battling droughts and other perilous impacts of climate change, the lack of any commitment to keep the rise in temperatures below 1.5 degrees C with firm action on phasing out fossil fuels was “a setback”.

“Panama cannot support this decision. One, because it repeats previously agreed commitments without closing the gap between reality and what science demands. Two, because it weighs too much upon technologies such as CCUS [carbon capture utilisation and storage] instead of calling for deep changes, and three, because it weakens language agreed in previous decisions. This is a setback, a rollback,” said Ana Aguilar, Panama’s chief climate negotiator.

On the other side, Saudi Arabia, China, and India are among the countries that are against explicit language on fossil fuel and expressed comfort with the way the cover text language was framed, while also expressing misgivings about the lack of clarity on adaptation finance. The countries are part of the Like Minded Developing Countries (LMDC) coalition, who are insistent on the use of fossil fuel in the foreseeable future to further their economies, but have also significantly deployed renewable energy.

Indian Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav said that India’s voice had shaped the draft COP 31 outcome, especially on food security, livelihoods, and cultural practices recognised in action on methane. However, in a post on X, he emphasised that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation. Energy transitions must be nationally determined, just and equitable, backed by finance, technology and capacity-building for developing countries.”

articles.title: Raut alleges BJP offers funds to secure support for Delimitation Bill
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Sanjay Raut alleged during the conference that an MP would receive ₹150 crore upon breaking away from a party to support the Delimitation Bill without facing disqualification

Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut alleged at a conference on November 22 that the Bharatiya Janata Party is offering ₹150 crore to Members of Parliament to gain backing for the Delimitation Bill, while also alleging that the government is delaying the session of the Parliament because it lacks the support of 40 to 45 MPs to pass the legislation and is attempting to pressure parties or buy lawmakers.
Editorial | Deservedly dead: On the defeat of the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026

The Delimitation Bill contains a provision to increase the number of seats in the Lok Sabha to 850, which has resulted in a dispute between the National Democratic Alliance and the INDIA bloc, where the National Democratic Alliance states that carrying out delimitation is required by the Constitution to reflect data from a census and to enable reservation for women, while the Opposition demands implementation of 33% reservation for women within a Lok Sabha that contains 543 members.

Sanjay Raut alleged during the conference that an MP would receive ₹150 crore upon breaking away from a party to support the Delimitation Bill without facing disqualification, and he claimed that a Minister from Maharashtra has taken responsibility for the situation and promised to provide funds for the purpose, further alleging that the government has delayed the session of the Parliament because it does not concern itself with the nation, the Constitution, or the Parliament, adding that if parties do not defect, MPs would be purchased, and he referenced a statement regarding a rate on an exchange of ₹150 crore per MP.
Shiv Sena-Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray / Bharatiya Janata Party / National Democratic Alliance

articles.title: 18th U.P. Legislative Assembly sits less than 90 days, experts point to unhealthy concentration of power in the Executive
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Fewer functioning days directly limit legislative oversight, and MLAs lose the chance to raise people-centric issues making legislature a passive spectator; experts call it contrary to spirit of constitutional checks and balance

With hardly two months left for Uttar Pradesh assembly polls and the 18 th Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly (May 2022- March 2027) nearing completion, question marks have been raised over the fewer days/meetings of the Legislative Assembly in the last five years.
Editorial | Stoop to conquer: On the Opposition’s seat-sharing ahead of U.P. polls

As the 18th Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly functioned for only 84 days, an average of 17 days a year, Opposition parties and constitutional experts in the State said fewer functioning days directly limit legislative oversight, and MLAs lose opportunities to raise constituency-centric issues.
They added that in a State having a population of over 25 crores (250 million people), at least 50 days of Assembly sessions per year, similar to the Lok Sabha, are necessary.

A House entrusted with representing more than 25 crore citizens reportedly sat for only 84 days over its five-year tenure, averaging just 17 sitting days a year. Such infrequent sittings are not a matter of administrative convenience; they strike at the heart of the constitutional scheme of accountable government. For a State grappling with enormous developmental challenges, law-and-order concerns and a population larger than that of most countries, such limited legislative engagement is indefensible. articles.title: Mumbai Police to issue cards with QR code for identity checks
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Devendra Fadnavis inaugurated the measure on November 21, 2026, and cards were distributed to personnel, including traffic police, as part of steps to digitise the force

Mumbai Police will issue cards with QR code and NFC to personnel, and citizens can scan the code through the Mumbai Police Citizen App to check a person’s photograph, name, date of joining and posting, a measure that follows cases in which fraudsters posed as police and sought money from citizens.

Devendra Fadnavis inaugurated the measure on Saturday (November 21, 2026), and cards were distributed to personnel, including traffic police, as part of steps to digitise the force. Mumbai Police states that printing has been completed, that personnel will receive cards within a month, that the project covers 51,308 posts and that the government sanctioned about ₹4 crore in February.

Personnel must carry the card while on duty, in uniform or not; officers who visit premises where people live, question citizens or approach people during investigations will have to carry it, so that those whom they approach can verify credentials; and a scan through the app directs users to a platform that displays photograph, name, date of joining and posting, which citizens can compare with the person who presents the card.

The card will have NFC technology, which personnel with authorisation can use for access to police establishments and for purposes, and the measure comes against a pattern in which criminals use cards that carry police identity and claim to be from crime branch to intimidate people into handing over cash or valuables, with fraudsters stopping citizens during walks and businessmen while claiming to conduct checks.

The system could offer a means of verification in scams in which fraudsters pose as police, CBI or officials from law enforcement during video calls and circulate cards with identity to establish credibility, and citizens can check credentials of anyone who claims to be a Mumbai Police officer rather than rely on a card.
Mr. Fadnavis said criminals use technology and police must stay ahead, and that technology works without bias and can improve efficiency.

Devendra Fadnavis inaugurated the measure on Saturday (November 21, 2026), and cards were distributed to personnel, including traffic police, as part of steps to digitise the force. Mumbai Police states that printing has been completed, that personnel will receive cards within a month, that the project covers 51,308 posts and that the government sanctioned about ₹4 crore in February.

Personnel must carry the card while on duty, in uniform or not; officers who visit premises where people live, question citizens or approach people during investigations will have to carry it, so that those whom they approach can verify credentials; and a scan through the app directs users to a platform that displays photograph, name, date of joining and posting, which citizens can compare with the person who presents the card.

The card will have NFC technology, which personnel with authorisation can use for access to police establishments and for purposes, and the measure comes against a pattern in which criminals use cards that carry police identity and claim to be from crime branch to intimidate people into handing over cash or valuables, with fraudsters stopping citizens during walks and businessmen while claiming to conduct checks.

The system could offer a means of verification in scams in which fraudsters pose as police, CBI or officials from law enforcement during video calls and circulate cards with identity to establish credibility, and citizens can check credentials of anyone who claims to be a Mumbai Police officer rather than rely on a card.

Nine people were shot at a concert in central California, leaving one person critically injured with a chest injury, the local sheriff said Sunday (November 22).

The shooting broke out around 7:30 p.m. Saturday (November 21) at a concert attended by about 150 people in Strathmore, a small town in Tulare County, a mountainous region in the centre of the state, the county sheriff's department said in a statement. An unspecified number of suspects opened fire on the crowd. No arrests were announced.

One 26-year-old man was shot in the chest and required surgery. He remained in critical condition, the sheriff's department said. Two other victims, ages 19 and 22, also required surgery, while six people sustained minor injuries.

Authorities said that they believe the shooting “may be gang-related” but didn't elaborate. The show in the town of roughly 3,000 people featured performers from neighbouring states, the department said.
The department didn't immediately respond to emailed questions seeking further details but said there was no longer any immediate threat to the public.

articles.title: West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya calls for protest over attacks on Hindus in Bangladesh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: State BJP chief claims Bangladesh was created on the basis of religion, not language, as Bengali-speaking Hindus are now being persecuted and bearing the consequences of Partition
West Bengal Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) president Samik Bhattacharya on Sunday (November 22, 2026) called for a protest against the alleged persecution of Hindus in Bangladesh .
“Blood is being shed in Bangladesh, and it is our brothers who are suffering. As a Bengali Hindu, I believe we must take to the streets,” the BJP leader told media persons.

Noting that India had played a crucial role in the creation of Bangladesh, the BJP Rajya Sabha MP expressed his opinion that Bangladesh was created on the basis of religion, not on the basis of the Bengali language.

“Bangladesh was not created for the sake of language. If it had been, Bengali-speaking Hindus in Bangladesh would not be dying like this today,” he said. Mr. Bhattacharya said that the fundamental question at that time should have been the protection of people and the creation of a democratic environment. Instead, the leadership surrendered to religious fundamentalism, he said.

Claiming that the wounds of Partition continued to haunt the subcontinent, the BJP leader said that it was religious minorities, particularly Hindus in Bangladesh, who were bearing the consequences. Blaming Partition on Jawaharlal Nehru and Mahatma Gandhi, Mr. Bhattacharya claimed that had Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose become independent India’s first Prime Minister, he would never have accepted the two-nation theory or allowed the subcontinent to be divided into India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh.

The remarks by the West Bengal BJP leader come at a time when fresh political tensions have erupted in Bangladesh. Attempts at normalising the India-Bangladesh relationship in recent months have been hindered by former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s presence in India, where she took refuge on August 5, 2024. Ms. Hasina has announced that she is keen to return to Bangladesh.

articles.title: FSSAI orders prosecution against Bisleri International for unsafe packaged drinking water
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: "The sample was found non-compliant with the prescribed bromate limits and declared unsafe under the FSS Act, 2006," the regulator said
Food regulator FSSAI on Sunday (November 22, 2026) said it has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International, as it found its sample of packaged drinking water "unsafe".
In a social media post, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said it has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd regarding "unsafe packaged drinking water".
A regulatory sample of "Packaged Drinking Water (other than Mineral Water)" was collected from the premises of Bisleri International for analysis.
"The sample was found non-compliant with the prescribed bromate limits and declared unsafe under the FSS Act, 2006," the regulator said.
Upon appeal by the company, the sample was sent to the referral food laboratory, which also declared it "unsafe" due to the detection of polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), the regulator added.

The findings of the lab established violations relating to unsafe food under the law. Hence, the FSSAI said it has granted sanction to launch prosecution under the FSS Act, 2006, against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd.

Through a social media post, FSSAI said it has sanctioned prosecution against a few other companies, including Vasant Masala Pvt Ltd, Tit-Bit Foods India Pvt Ltd, Mimansa Industries and Asha Confectionery.
The regulator has suspended the licence of Urmi Lifesciences LLP and Gaur Ayurvedic Store for non-compliance of rules and regulations.
FSSAI has also issued a product recall order against Asha Confectionery. The company has been asked to withdraw pre-pack chocolate filled cookies as they were found unsafe.

In a social media post, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said it has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd regarding "unsafe packaged drinking water".

A regulatory sample of "Packaged Drinking Water (other than Mineral Water)" was collected from the premises of Bisleri International for analysis.

"The sample was found non-compliant with the prescribed bromate limits and declared unsafe under the FSS Act, 2006," the regulator said.

Upon appeal by the company, the sample was sent to the referral food laboratory, which also declared it "unsafe" due to the detection of polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), the regulator added.

The findings of the lab established violations relating to unsafe food under the law. Hence, the FSSAI said it has granted sanction to launch prosecution under the FSS Act, 2006, against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd.

Through a social media post, FSSAI said it has sanctioned prosecution against a few other companies, including Vasant Masala Pvt Ltd, Tit-Bit Foods India Pvt Ltd, Mimansa Industries and Asha Confectionery.

The regulator has suspended the licence of Urmi Lifesciences LLP and Gaur Ayurvedic Store for non-compliance of rules and regulations.

FSSAI has also issued a product recall order against Asha Confectionery. The company has been asked to withdraw pre-pack chocolate filled cookies as they were found unsafe.

articles.title: SIR: Voters in Karnataka challenge deletions, say officials asking them to withdraw appeals, file Form 6
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Hindu spoke to several people in Bengaluru who challenged their deletion, some of whom said officials had themselves submitted Form 6 applications on their behalf when they approached them seeking reversal of their deletion through an appeal

After the final electoral rolls from the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) were published, several people whose names had been deleted challenged their exclusion. They argued that they were left out despite having completed the entire process, including attending hearings and submitting the required documents.

More than 350 appeals have been filed across Karnataka so far. The Deputy Commissioner or District Election Officer (DEO) serves as the first appellate authority in the SIR, while the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) is the second and final appellate authority if the first-stage response is unsatisfactory. According to the CEO’s office, all appeals received so far remain pending or have been disposed of at the first appellate stage.

The Hindu spoke to several people in Bengaluru who have challenged their deletion. While some said officials advised them to withdraw their appeals and apply afresh through Form 6, others said officials had themselves submitted Form 6 applications on their behalf when they approached them seeking reversal of their deletion through an appeal. A few of them said they had since received an Elector’s Photo Identity Card (EPIC) and were told that their names would figure in a supplementary list.

While Form 6 applications are accepted throughout the year as part of the ECI’s “continuous updation” process, this route could leave those excluded from the SIR rolls unable to vote in the upcoming local body elections, including the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) elections. The GBA elections have been directed to be conducted using the SIR final rolls by December, before even the summary revision process begins or a supplementary list is published.

Those who have appealed argue that they are not new voters seeking fresh inclusion, but people who have been voting from the same addresses and were wrongly deleted. They also questioned why they should be asked to make a declaration through Form 6 that does not reflect their circumstances, when they had already submitted documents to address the discrepancies flagged during the SIR.

Iqbal, a resident of Sarjapura, told The Hindu that he received a notice over “no mapping.” He had mapped his father’s details, whose name is on the electoral roll in Bihar,but his name was still flagged. Mr. Iqbal said that although he had shifted his residence within the city more than five years ago, his EPIC had been updated and he had submitted the required documents. His name was deleted from the final SIR rolls after figuring in the draft list.

Several people also said that while the names of all members of their families figured in the draft rolls, some were deleted from the final list. They argued that even when appeals were disposed of, the outcomes were not uniform within families.

Sahiba, a resident of Jayanagar, said she was flagged over an anomaly indicating that the age gap between two children was less than nine months. She has twins and submitted their birth certificates to establish this. However, officials subsequently raised a discrepancy in her mother’s name across records. “I explained that it was the same person and that only the spelling had changed during translation. I submitted all my documents as well as my mother’s. But I was then questioned about why I had mapped to my mother and not my father or husband. Both my father and husband are in Saudi Arabia and were not part of the 2002 rolls. Now the officials are telling me to withdraw my appeal and file Form 6,” she said.

She reportedly intended to visit the bungalow along with her mother, Y.S. Vijayalakshmi.

The police informed Ms. Sharmila about the interim injunction order, which restrains her from entering the disputed property. The court order also prohibits her family members, agents, representatives and anyone acting on her behalf from obstructing or interfering with the property.

articles.title: Suspected Ukrainian sea drones hit Russian warship at Benghazi naval base, Libyan officials say
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The strike at the Benghazi Naval Base in eastern Libya severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette, and ignited a fire at the facility, two Libyan military officials said

A suspected Ukrainian drone strike hit a Russian warship on Sunday (November 22, 2026) at a naval base in Libya, officials said, the latest attack in the North African nation linked to the Russia-Ukraine war.
The strike at the Benghazi Naval Base in eastern Libya severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette, and ignited a fire at the facility, two Libyan military officials said.

They said that several Ukrainian sea drones were launched at the ship from a base run by Ukrainian forces in western Libya, according to an initial investigation into the attack. At least four drones were intercepted and destroyed, while two hit the warship, they said.
The officials, affiliated with the self-styled Libyan National Army, which controls eastern and southern Libya, spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren't allowed to talk with reporters.

Libya has been divided since a NATO-backed uprising toppled longtime dictator Muammar Gaddafi, who was later killed, in 2011. A UN-supported government is based in Tripoli, and a rival administration is located in the east. The oil-rich nation remains a focal point for a long-running rivalry between Russia and the West.
The eastern Libya-based government said in a statement that the strike on Sunday (November 22) caused an explosion and fire at the base, which was later extinguished.

The Almasar satellite television channel aired footage showing a vessel erupting into flames. It said the Libyan navy rescued the crew of the Maltese-flagged ship. A corvette is a warship smaller than a frigate or destroyer and is built to patrol coastal waters and escort other ships.

The vessel had docked at the Libyan base for refuelling and supplies as part of a cooperation agreement between Russia and the eastern-based government in Libya, the statement said, without providing details on the vessel or its cargo.
A joint investigation was launched with Russia to “uncover the circumstances of the attack, its source, and the party behind it,” the statement said.
No group immediately claimed responsibility for the attack. There was no immediate comment from either Russia or Ukraine.

articles.title: Israel’s Eisenkot condemns arson attacks by Jewish settlers in West Bank
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Gadi Eisenkot called the attacks ‘Jewish terrorism’, saying that ‘extremist groups that set ⁠fire to vehicles and homes are undermining regional stability, putting lives at risk and doing grave damage to Israel’s national security and foreign relations’

Israeli militant settlers attacked Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank ‌early on Sunday (November 22, 2026), starting fires and scrawling racist graffiti, residents said, prompting an ​accusation of “Jewish terrorism” from the man trying to form an Israeli government.

The attacks come nearly a month after an inconclusive election stripped incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of his ‌majority. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has been asked to form a government, though his prospects seem little better.

Reuters saw burned-out Palestinian vehicles and walls spray-painted with slogans ‌such as “Revenge” and “Death to Arabs” in villages near Ramallah. No one immediately claimed responsibility and ‌no ⁠injuries were reported.

Mr. Eisenkot called the attacks “Jewish terrorism”, saying that “extremist groups that set ⁠fire to vehicles and homes are undermining regional stability, putting lives at risk and doing grave damage to Israel’s national security and foreign relations”.

He said the policies of Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, ultra-nationalist ministers in Mr. Netanyahu’s cabinet, had “brought the ​area to the brink of anarchy, ‌and the authorities have yet to address the crisis”.

Mr. Netanyahu has not yet commented, but Foreign Minister Gideon Saar condemned the attacks by a “handful of extremists” and said they are “against our values and do not represent the law-abiding citizens of Judea and Samaria” — the biblical ‌names for the West Bank.
“Israeli authorities are firmly committed to enforcing the law against extremist ​violence,” he told the ELNET Jerusalem Summit.
UN bodies and most countries of the world deny the legality of the settlements, which make the ⁠prospect of an independent Palestinian state ever more remote, a position Israel disputes.

Israeli police said they opened an investigation into the attacks, while the military condemned the violence, saying soldiers and police ‌had been dispatched to the areas of Deir as-Sudan, Deir Abu Masha’al, Kafr Malik and At-Tuwani “following reports and footage showing vehicles being set on fire and graffiti being sprayed in the area”.

Mr. Ben-Gvir replied in an X post that Mr. Eisenkot’s condemnation amounted to selling out to Arab parties, which could become part of a possible new government. Mr. Smotrich favours settlement expansion and wants Israel to annex the West Bank.

articles.title: Japan-Europe spacecraft BepiColombo begins orbit of Mercury, with a glitch reported
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The mission will seek to answer questions about Mercury such as why it has a magnetic field, why ice exists in the polar craters of a sun-scorched planet, and what is the nature of enigmatic depressions called "hollows" on its surface

After an eight-year journey, the European-Japanese spacecraft BepiColombo has begun orbiting the solar system's smallest ​and innermost planet Mercury, though the European Space Agency said ‌on Sunday (November 22, 2026) a glitch has occurred involving its thrusters.

Mercury, ​only slightly larger than Earth's moon, ⁠is the least explored of the four planets in the inner solar system, with BepiColombo only the third spacecraft to visit the ‌planet and just the second to orbit it.
It is a joint mission of the European Space ‌Agency, or ESA, and the Japan Aerospace Exploration ‌Agency, ⁠or JAXA.

ESA confirmed on Saturday (November 21) that BepiColombo ⁠had begun its orbit. In a social media post on Sunday (November 22), ESA said the spacecraft had a successful entry into orbit, but during the ​manoeuver, "the thruster burn was shorter ‌than planned following a software issue."
"The spacecraft is safe and teams at ESOC (the European Space Operations Centre) are working to understand what happened," ESA said, adding that "updates will ‌be provided on Monday."

The robotic spacecraft, launched in ​2018, is a composite of ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, which have different ⁠scientific objectives and are due to separate on December 9 and 10. Routine science operations are slated to commence ‌in April.

The mission will seek to answer questions about Mercury such as why it has a magnetic field, why ice exists in the polar craters of a sun-scorched planet, and what is the nature of enigmatic depressions called "hollows" on its surface.
Mercury's surface looks similar to that ‌of the Moon, with numerous impact craters. There are expanses of ​smooth terrain as well as cliffs, some up to a mile (1.6 km) tall.

Mercury is about 60% ⁠closer to the Sun than Earth. That means that from ⁠its surface, the Sun appears more than three times as large and seven times as luminous ‌as it does when seen from Earth. Mercury's diameter of 3,032 miles (4,880 km) is less than 40% of ​Earth's diameter of 7,926 miles (12,753 km).

After an eight-year journey, the European-Japanese spacecraft BepiColombo has begun orbiting the solar system's smallest ​and innermost planet Mercury, though the European Space Agency said ‌on Sunday (November 22, 2026) a glitch has occurred involving its thrusters.

Mercury, ​only slightly larger than Earth's moon, ⁠is the least explored of the four planets in the inner solar system, with BepiColombo only the third spacecraft to visit the ‌planet and just the second to orbit it.

It is a joint mission of the European Space ‌Agency, or ESA, and the Japan Aerospace Exploration ‌Agency, ⁠or JAXA.

ESA confirmed on Saturday (November 21) that BepiColombo ⁠had begun its orbit. In a social media post on Sunday (November 22), ESA said the spacecraft had a successful entry into orbit, but during the ​manoeuver, "the thruster burn was shorter ‌than planned following a software issue."

"The spacecraft is safe and teams at ESOC (the European Space Operations Centre) are working to understand what happened," ESA said, adding that "updates will ‌be provided on Monday."

The robotic spacecraft, launched in ​2018, is a composite of ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, which have different ⁠scientific objectives and are due to separate on December 9 and 10. Routine science operations are slated to commence ‌in April.

The mission will seek to answer questions about Mercury such as why it has a magnetic field, why ice exists in the polar craters of a sun-scorched planet, and what is the nature of enigmatic depressions called "hollows" on its surface.

Mercury's surface looks similar to that ‌of the Moon, with numerous impact craters. There are expanses of ​smooth terrain as well as cliffs, some up to a mile (1.6 km) tall.

Mercury is about 60% ⁠closer to the Sun than Earth. That means that from ⁠its surface, the Sun appears more than three times as large and seven times as luminous ‌as it does when seen from Earth. articles.title: Anthropic IPO: Tracing an ‘unusual’ AI company’s race to the top
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Set up as a Public Benefit Corporation, Anthropic warns that AI could be dangerous, yet races to build the most powerful models. Charts and a timeline unpack the journey and contradictions of the AI company behind the largest-ever IPO

Minutes before Anthropic, the maker of Claude, began trading on Nasdaq on November 19, its co-founder and president Daniela Amodei opened her short speech by calling it an “unusual” company, one many even call “weird”.

Founded in May 2021 by seven former OpenAI employees who left over what they saw as a culture that did not put AI safety and alignment first, Anthropic is registered as a Public Benefit Corporation (PBC), a structure that legally binds the company to weigh public benefit alongside profit.

Its CEO Dario Amodei has consistently warned about the existential risks of misaligned AI models and pushed for regulation and a slowdown in the race to build frontier models. Rivals and some critics, however, have called this posturing. The provocatively titled “MisAnthropic Statement”, released on the eve of the IPO and signed by a few prominent figures from different fields, said Anthropic was not a safe AI company and urged rejection of its “reckless attempt to amass power in the name of the greater good”.
The charts and timeline below trace the unconventional journey of a company seen as a harbinger of everything unusual unfolding in the AI zeitgeist.

Anthropic raised $81.3 billion despite listing during a market slump — with many beginning to wonder whether the ballooning investments in AI were a bubble — and against the backdrop of the Republican rout in the U.S. midterms and the Nvidia scandal. It broke the record for the largest-ever IPO, set by Elon Musk’s SpaceX just five months earlier in a more bullish market.

articles.title: Scientists report strong new evidence that specially bred mosquitoes can fend off dengue
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The latest research comes as Florida grapples with an unusually large outbreak of the virus, what appears to be the biggest in any U.S. state since at least the 1940s
Children who lived in Brazilian neighbourhoods buzzing with a special kind of mosquito were far less likely to catch dengue or another worrisome virus, chikungunya, researchers reported Saturday.

The major study of more than 5,700 children in one of the world's dengue hot spots offers new evidence that breeding mosquitoes unable to transmit these viruses can be a viable strategy rather than solely relying on pesticides and trying to avoid getting bitten.

In neighbourhoods populated by these so-called Wolbachia-carrying mosquitoes, researchers found about a 69% reduction in dengue and chikungunya infections in schoolchildren compared to similar neighbourhoods — an effect sustained even during Brazil's severe 2024 dengue outbreak, said Dr. Sri Edupuganti of Emory University, part of the international research team.
The researchers reported the findings at a meeting of the American Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene.

“This is really exciting,” said David Hamer, a global health expert at Boston University who wasn't involved with the Brazilian study. He predicts that pairing more use of these Wolbachia mosquitoes with existing steps to fight mosquito-borne disease could “knock dengue down to much lower levels” in many places.
The latest research comes as Florida grapples with an unusually large outbreak of the virus, what appears to be the biggest in any U.S. state since at least the 1940s.

Usually in the continental US, dengue is found mostly in people who travelled internationally. But as of Friday, Florida health officials had tallied more than 650 locally acquired cases, about three-quarters of them in Hillsborough County, home to Tampa.
Outside the U.S., the nonprofit World Mosquito Program has pioneered the Wolbachia strategy.

How it works: Scientists breed mosquitoes to carry a kind of bacteria called Wolbachia. It is harmless to people and common in many insects, although not dengue-carrying Aedes aegypti mosquitoes. The bacteria dramatically reduce the mosquitoes' ability to transmit certain viruses. Female mosquitoes spread the bacteria to their offspring, so releasing enough of the specially bred insects — males and females — into an area allows Wolbachia to gradually become established in the local mosquito population.

Field trials and other studies in Indonesia and elsewhere have shown the strategy can significantly lower dengue diagnoses. But because people with mild symptoms may not be diagnosed, the new study in Belo Horizonte, Brazil, went further. Researchers tested blood for signs of dengue, chikungunya or the Zika virus.

The latest research comes as Florida grapples with an unusually large outbreak of the virus, what appears to be the biggest in any U.S. state since at least the 1940s.

Usually in the continental US, dengue is found mostly in people who travelled internationally. But as of Friday, Florida health officials had tallied more than 650 locally acquired cases, about three-quarters of them in Hillsborough County, home to Tampa.

Outside the U.S., the nonprofit World Mosquito Program has pioneered the Wolbachia strategy.

How it works: Scientists breed mosquitoes to carry a kind of bacteria called Wolbachia. It is harmless to people and common in many insects, although not dengue-carrying Aedes aegypti mosquitoes. The bacteria dramatically reduce the mosquitoes' ability to transmit certain viruses. Female mosquitoes spread the bacteria to their offspring, so releasing enough of the specially bred insects — males and females — into an area allows Wolbachia to gradually become established in the local mosquito population.

Field trials and other studies in Indonesia and elsewhere have shown the strategy can significantly lower dengue diagnoses. But because people with mild symptoms may not be diagnosed, the new study in Belo Horizonte, Brazil, went further. Researchers tested blood for signs of dengue, chikungunya or the Zika virus.

articles.title: DRDO scientist P.C. Jain receives Murli Manohar Joshi Award
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: An alumnus of IIT Roorkee and IIT Bombay, Prakash Chand Jain’s work resulted in substantial weight reductions in missile airframes

Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) scientist Prakash Chand Jain has been awarded the Dr. Murli Manohar Joshi Award in the Science and Technology category for his contributions to the structural design of missile systems and for strengthening India’s defence research capabilities.

Mr. Jain, an outstanding scientist at the Defence Research and Development Laboratory (DRDL) in the Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Missile Complex, Hyderabad, received the award from former Union Minister Murli Manohar Joshi in New Delhi on Sunday (November 22).
Instituted by the Federation for World Academics (FWA), the award recognises contributions to scientific research, technological innovation and their societal impact.

An alumnus of IIT Roorkee and IIT Bombay, Jain has made significant contributions to structural optimisation, resulting in substantial weight reductions in missile airframes. His research covers vibration analysis and complex structural challenges in aerospace engineering.

articles.title: PM Modi holds bilateral talks with Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah; trade, investment, connectivity on agenda
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah, on a two-day State visit, laid a wreath at Raj Ghat and received a Guard of Honour at Rashtrapati Bhavan before the talks at Hyderabad House

Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah arrived at Hyderabad House on Monday (November 23, 2026) to hold bilateral talks, to review India-Nepal relations and explore avenues for strengthening cooperation across key sectors.
The discussions are expected to focus on strengthening economic cooperation, particularly in trade, transportation, investment and infrastructure development.

Both countries are also expected to exchange memorandums of understanding (MoUs) covering several areas of mutual interest, including education, health, agriculture, sports, disaster management and human resource development. Connectivity and energy cooperation are also expected to feature prominently during the visit.

The two sides are expected to inaugurate several completed projects in these sectors and lay foundation stones for upcoming initiatives, reflecting their efforts to expand cross-border cooperation. Beyond government-level engagements, the visit will also feature a Nepal-India Business Forum aimed at attracting Indian investment to Nepal.
The forum will provide a platform for business representatives from both countries to explore opportunities for collaboration and strengthen commercial ties.

Mr. Modi will also host an official luncheon in honour of Mr. Shah and his 34-member government delegation. The Nepal Prime Minister is accompanied by Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle, Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal, Chief Advisor to the Prime Minister Kumar Byanjankar and other senior government officials.

Earlier in the day, Mr. Shah paid tribute to Mahatma Gandhi, by laying a wreath at his memorial at Raj Ghat, as part of his State visit to India. He also signed the guestbook at the memorial. Before this, he received a ceremonial Guard of Honour at Rashtrapati Bhavan, with Mr. Modi in attendance.

The two-day State visit is expected to provide an opportunity for both sides to take stock of their bilateral partnership, review ongoing cooperation and explore ways to expand engagement across areas of shared interest.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah arrived at Hyderabad House on Monday (November 23, 2026) to hold bilateral talks, to review India-Nepal relations and explore avenues for strengthening cooperation across key sectors.

The discussions are expected to focus on strengthening economic cooperation, particularly in trade, transportation, investment and infrastructure development.

Both countries are also expected to exchange memorandums of understanding (MoUs) covering several areas of mutual interest, including education, health, agriculture, sports, disaster management and human resource development. The forum will provide a platform for business representatives from both countries to explore opportunities for collaboration and strengthen commercial ties.

Mr. Modi will also host an official luncheon in honour of Mr. Shah and his 34-member government delegation. The Nepal Prime Minister is accompanied by Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle, Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal, Chief Advisor to the Prime Minister Kumar Byanjankar and other senior government officials.

Earlier in the day, Mr. Shah paid tribute to Mahatma Gandhi, by laying a wreath at his memorial at Raj Ghat, as part of his State visit to India. He also signed the guestbook at the memorial. Before this, he received a ceremonial Guard of Honour at Rashtrapati Bhavan, with Mr. Modi in attendance.

articles.title: Lights out after defeat: 50 streetlights disappear from village after BJP candidate loses in Rajasthan’s Tonk
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: However, Govardhan Choudhary, assistant engineer with the electricity department in Peeplu, said the streetlights had been installed without authorisation and were removed in accordance with departmental policy

Hours after a BJP candidate lost the Panchayat Samiti elections, around 50 streetlights installed in a village in Rajasthan’s Tonk district were removed by electricity department workers, according to villagers.

However, Govardhan Choudhary, assistant engineer with the electricity department in Peeplu, said the streetlights had been installed without authorisation and were removed in accordance with departmental policy.
The incident took place in Ward 2 of Peeplu Panchayat Samiti, where BJP candidate Priyanka Sharma lost to her Congress rival Dhanna Lal by 751 votes.
Ms. Priyanka is the wife of Alok Sharma, personal assistant to BJP MLA Ram Sahay Verma of Niwai constituency.
According to villagers, the streetlights were installed on October 24 during the election campaign to illuminate streets and residential areas that had remained dark after sunset.
A few hours after the results were declared on Friday (November 20, 2026), electricity department workers arrived in a vehicle and removed the lights.
“The lights were installed in an unauthorised manner,” Mr. Choudhary said, adding that similar action would be taken against unauthorised streetlights in other wards.

Villagers questioned the timing of the action, alleging that the lights were removed because the BJP candidate had lost the election. They said the installations had provided relief from darkness and were appreciated by residents.
MLA Ramsahay Verma denied that he or his personal assistant’s wife had any role in the removal of the lights.
Rajasthan / Bharatiya Janata Party / local elections / Indian National Congress

articles.title: Nepal PM India visit LIVE: Balen Shah begins bilateral visit; energy, connectivity on agenda
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: This is Balen Shah's first official bilateral foreign visit since taking office in March. He travelled to the U.S. in September to attend the United Nations General Assembly

Saryu-Kamala Express, which will run between Ayodhya and Janakpur, Nepal, was inaugurated today at the Ayodhya Cantt Railway Station via video conferencing by PM Narendra Modi and Nepal PM Balen Shah.

Nepal PM Balendra Shah after paying homage to Mahatma Gandhi at Raj Ghat today, wrote in the memorial’s visitor book describing truth as “a power unmatched by any force” and calling compassion “the ultimate strength”.

Linking Gandhi’s legacy with Nepal’s heritage, the Nepalese PM added, “On behalf of the people and Government of Nepal, I offer my deepest tribute. Coming from the birthplace of Lord Buddha, I behold in Gandhiji’s legacy that very same immortal light: the profound truth that compassion is the ultimate strength, and that true leadership lies in selfless service to the humblest among us.”

The Ministry of External Affairs said, “India and Nepal share close and friendly relations, rooted in historical, cultural and civilisational links and strong people-to-people ties. Bilateral cooperation has witnessed progress across diverse sectors, including trade and commerce, development partnership, energy and water resources, and physical and digital connectivity, with growing engagement in newer areas such as start-ups, technology and innovation, and sports”.
Prime Minister Modi will also host an official luncheon in honour of his Nepalese counterpart and his 34-member government delegation.

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said the start of a direct rail service between Ayodhya and Janakpur in Nepal will open a new chapter in the centuries-old spiritual and cultural ties between the two regions and would strengthen India-Nepal relations and facilitate pilgrimage for crores of devotees.

India and Nepal discussions are expected to focus on strengthening economic cooperation, particularly in trade, transportation, investment and infrastructure development. Both countries are also expected to exchange memorandums of understanding (MoUs) covering several areas of mutual interest, including education, health, agriculture, sports, disaster management and human resource development.

Connectivity and energy cooperation are also expected to feature prominently during the visit. The two sides are expected to inaugurate several completed projects in these sectors and lay foundation stones for upcoming initiatives, reflecting their efforts to expand cross-border cooperation.

Former Nepal PM Jhala Nath Khanal said Nepal and India should maintain cordial relations and expand comprehensive cooperation, while expressing concern that Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah had not prepared a common national agenda ahead of his ongoing visit to India.

“There are many expectations. And there are some irritants also in our relations which have to be eliminated. And the relations between our two countries should be comprehensively developed based on five principles of peaceful coexistence and neighbourliness,” Mr. Khanal said.

articles.title: In 12 states, NGO Pratham’s Second Chance Programme is helping women school dropouts appear for their Class X Board exams
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: As a significant percentage of older girls and women in India have not completed secondary education, this 14-year-old initiative focuses on helping them restart their educational journey and direct it towards earning a livelihood

In a tranquil residential enclave at Vijaypura in Devanahalli, 40 kilometres from Bengaluru city, a modest abode has been converted into a classroom, the walls supporting a mixed population of subjects: on one patch of a wall, Kannada vowels and consonants and scientific diagrams enjoy joint tenancy.

Women frantically take down notes as the blackboard gets busy. From time to time, someone would look up from the note-taking to clarify doubts. At this hour, the doubts pertain to monohybrid cross and dihybrid cross. Navyanthi D.N., the science teacher, offers patient answers.

It is a motley class of learners, consisting of Asha workers, a tailor, a young mother with a toddler on her lap watching the phone, noon meal staff working in schools, and determined homemakers in good numbers. An employee with the Kempegowda International Airport makes a dash for the door around noon; she had sought permission to leave the class early to be present at work.

This is one of the many learning clusters run as part of the Pratham-Jameel Second Chance programme, an initiative by the Pratham Education Foundation, to support girls and women who have dropped out of school before completing secondary education. At the Devanahalli Block, this programme is in its second year.

Approximately 24 lakh students fail in Class X every year, and a vast number of them drop out of the formal education system, says a study from the Ministry of Education. Efforts to get them to progress to Class XI through the National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS) meet with modest success. An analysis report by the Ministry of Education, published in The Hindu in May 2023, states the failure rates range between 47% and 55%.
Given this, interventions by NGOs such as Pratham become significant and essential. Pratham has been bringing out the ASER (Annual Status of Education Report) since 2005.

Started in 2011 as a pilot in Maharashtra, the Second Chance Programme was extended to seven states. Currently, it is being run in 12 states, including Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Rajasthan, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka.

After many door-to-door mobilisation campaigns to enrol women candidates, the new academic year of the Second Chance Programme began in July 2026 in most cities. The foundation course, typically covering lessons taught in the upper middle classes, soaks up three to four months.
Mothers’ groups in neighbourhoods help the ground staff get information about other women or older girls who might be interested in completing class X.

Their ground staff’s tasks include persuading family members to support the women to pursue studies and have a secondary school leaving certificate no matter what the age of the person is. The persuasion sometimes has to be targeted at the women who have to take up the studies.

articles.title: Ukraine says Russian strikes kill 15 in Kyiv region
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Moscow has been pummelling Ukraine with nightly aerial barrages as the war-torn country braces for another winter, as the full-scale invasion grinds through its fifth year

Rescuers in Ukraine raced on Monday (November 23, 2026) to find residents trapped under the rubble of a block of flats that partially collapsed in a Russian strike, a fter attacks on the Kyiv region killed at least 15 people.
Moscow has been pummelling Ukraine with nightly aerial barrages as the war-torn country braces for another winter, as the full-scale invasion grinds through its fifth year.
Russian President Vladimir Putin vowed last week a "painful" response to Ukrainian strikes on Russia's Crimea bridge after holding a summit with U.S. counterpart Donald Trump and China's Xi Jinping.

An overnight strike on Dymer, around 45 kilometres (30 miles) north of the Ukrainian capital, hit a five-storey building, killing at least 11 people, according to Kyiv regional official Tymur Tkachenko.
AFP images showed rescuers combing through the mound of smouldering rubble.
"Rescuers recovered the body of another person from beneath the rubble," Tkachenko wrote on Telegram, confirming the death toll had risen to 11.
Ukraine's State Emergency Service said earlier on Telegram that the dead included a teenager and a woman in her forties.
It said earlier that rescuers were searching for 11 people, including two children, who were "not responding or cannot be reached".
Rescuers had managed to pull out people from the rubble including a 79-year-old woman and a child, Tkachenko said.
Ukrainian human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets called the attack part of "Russia's genocidal war against Ukraine".

articles.title: U.S. panel urges India dialogue for Dalai Lama succession, warns of China legitimacy contest
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: A U.S. Congressional panel has recommended establishing a senior-level channel with India for succession contingency planning for the 14th Dalai Lama, arguing that China may turn the process into an international legitimacy contest

A U.S. Congressional panel has recommended setting up a senior-level channel with India for succession contingency planning for the 14th Dalai Lama, contending that China may turn the process into an international contest over legitimacy.

A U.S. Congressional panel has recommended establishing a senior-level channel with India for succession contingency planning for the 14th Dalai Lama, arguing that China may turn the process into an international legitimacy contest.

The U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission, in a report to the U.S. Congress, made a strong pitch to recognise the Gaden Phodrang Trust as the sole legitimate authority to identify and recognise the successor to the 14th Dalai Lama.
The report by the bipartisan Commission said China was likely to use coercive tools to shape the outcome of the succession process.
It said that the U.S. Congress should adopt a policy of not recognising any successor to the Dalai Lama who is selected or installed by China.

“To carry out this policy and ensure U.S. government readiness for the Dalai Lama’s succession, Congress should direct the Secretary of State to… establish a senior-level channel with the Government of India for succession contingency planning, including intelligence sharing on Chinese influence operations,” the report said.

It also asked the U.S. Secretary of State to lead an internal interagency tabletop exercise on succession scenarios, with participation by the National Security Advisor, the Director of National Intelligence, and the Secretary of Defence.

The commission also asked the U.S. Secretary of State to conduct Track 1.5 and Track 2 dialogues and tabletop exercises with Indian counterparts on the political and security implications of succession scenarios.
The Commission also wanted the U.S. to coordinate with allies and partners on a diplomatic response that denies international legitimacy to any successor selected by China.

It also wanted the U.S. to counter succession-related influence operations by strengthening the Central Tibetan Administration’s cybersecurity and resilience against China’s cyber and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled disinformation campaigns.
