🌐 International & Geopolitics 📅 22 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

📰 COP 31 talks fail as EU, others reject any climate deal without language on a fossil fuel phase-out

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

EU, Panama among about 130 parties that refuse to accept COP President’s consensus cover text, alleges that it “greenwashes” fossil fuels; India, China, Saudi Arabia are on the other side of the divide

A standoff on a fossil fuel phase-out prevented countries at COP 31, the United Nations climate talks in Antalya, Turkiye, from achieving any consensus agreement on future climate action on Sunday (November 22, 2026), despite the conference running a record 48 hours into overtime.

The European Union led objections to COP 31 President Murat Kurum’s consensus cover text that failed to include any explicit language about moving away from fossil fuels. The EU’s stance was reportedly supported by about 130 countries.

On the other side of the divide, India is among the nations that supported the proposed cover text, as they want to keep using fossil fuels for the foreseeable future, with Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav stressing that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation.”

“We express profound disappointment with the final draft COP31 cover decision or Antalya Pact. At a point where the world urgently needs action to avert disastrous levels of global warming, the draft cover decision falls well short,” Ireland’s Climate Minister Darragh O’Brien said, speaking on behalf of the EU.

“We will not endorse a decision that does not respond to the science, that disregards the implementation gap, and that actually risks deepening the chasm between global commitments and the action required to correct the overshoot and bring 1.5 degrees back to within reach… We will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel,” he added.

A cover text is an overarching political decision that frames the outcome of a climate conference rather than settling any single agenda item. It is usually finalised last, and like every outcome, it needs the consensus of all parties.

Panama also formally objected to the text, saying that as a country battling droughts and other perilous impacts of climate change, the lack of any commitment to keep the rise in temperatures below 1.5 degrees C with firm action on phasing out fossil fuels was “a setback”.

“Panama cannot support this decision. One, because it repeats previously agreed commitments without closing the gap between reality and what science demands. Two, because it weighs too much upon technologies such as CCUS [carbon capture utilisation and storage] instead of calling for deep changes, and three, because it weakens language agreed in previous decisions. This is a setback, a rollback,” said Ana Aguilar, Panama’s chief climate negotiator.

On the other side, Saudi Arabia, China, and India are among the countries that are against explicit language on fossil fuel and expressed comfort with the way the cover text language was framed, while also expressing misgivings about the lack of clarity on adaptation finance. The countries are part of the Like Minded Developing Countries (LMDC) coalition, who are insistent on the use of fossil fuel in the foreseeable future to further their economies, but have also significantly deployed renewable energy.

Indian Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav said that India’s voice had shaped the draft COP 31 outcome, especially on food security, livelihoods, and cultural practices recognised in action on methane. However, in a post on X, he emphasised that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation. Energy transitions must be nationally determined, just and equitable, backed by finance, technology and capacity-building for developing countries.”

3. articles.title: Drone strikes hit homes, UN premises in Sudan's capital
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: A drone strike completely destroyed a house, a witness said, while a Sudanese Army source said the drones had been launched from Ethiopia
“Drones struck Sudan 's capital Khartoum, damaging residential homes and a United Nations building on Sunday (November 22, 2026),” witnesses and the world organisation said.

Explosions were heard in the area around Khartoum airport and other parts of the city from at around 2 a.m. until approximately 4:30 a.m. (0000-0230 GMT). A drone strike completely destroyed a house, a witness said, while a Sudanese Army source said the drones had been launched from Ethiopia.

"The drone attack at dawn today is a continuation of Ethiopian aggression against Sudanese territory, as the drones were launched from Ethiopia's Bahir Dar airport," the source told AFP . Sudan has repeatedly accused Ethiopia of allowing attacks to be launched from its territory, a claim Addis Ababa has denied.

Another witness reported that a drone hit the home of a mosque's muezzin, the person who calls Muslims to prayer, in Jebel Aulia, around 45 km (28 miles) south of Khartoum. "People were trying to rescue family members trapped under the rubble," the witness added.

The UN meanwhile said that "a UN premises with UN colleagues in the building was damaged". "This occurred in a civilian neighbourhood," the UN's Humanitarian Office (OCHA) said in a statement posted on X.
OCHA condemned the risk posed to humanitarian workers, saying it was "unacceptable" that UN personnel were being exposed to such danger. Authorities did not immediately report on casualties.

The conflict, which erupted in April 2023 between the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and the Sudanese Army, has killed more than 2,00,000 people, aid workers estimate, and triggered the world's largest hunger and displacement crises.
The United Nations has repeatedly criticised both sides' rampant use of drones, which killed more than 1,100 people in the first half of 2026.

“Of the hundreds of child casualties this year, two-thirds were killed or injured by drone strikes,” the UN said last week. A Sudanese Army drone strike killed 15 people, including four children, in a West Kordofan village days ago, as the Army pushed through the state, recapturing territory from the RSF.

The rival forces have for the last year wrestled for control of the resource-rich southern Kordofan region, which connects the Army-held centre and east to RSF-controlled Darfur. In recent months, both the Army and the RSF have increasingly relied on drones capable of striking targets hundreds of kilometres away without risking their fighters.

articles.title: Giving India’s first practising woman doctor her due: Kadambini Ganguly​
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Kadambini Ganguly broke barriers to become one of India’s first women physicians to practise Western medicine

As far as trailblazers go, Kadambini Ganguly will figure right on top of several lists. She was a pioneering woman physician, the first to practise successfully in India, a gynaecologist and a social reformer who, equally efficiently, managed a large family as well. The story of Kadambini Ganguly is one of extraordinary achievement, and if told widely, will continue to inspire the young women of today.

In a profile published in Cureus in 2024, the authors point to the influence of the progressive Bramho Samaj movement, initiated by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, that helped Kadambini emerge from the shackles of conservative orthodoxy that might have stiffled her immense talent. “This environment, which championed the values of education and gender equality, contributed significantly to shaping her exemplary career and lifelong dedication to social justice,” the article reads. Records of her life acknowledge that she was partly recognised during her lifetime, but also mercilessly criticised and defamed for being a progressive, working woman. The full recognition of her contributions in medicine and the social sector came much later, only in recent decades.

fullParagraphs: Rampur Bushahr’s Lavi Fair in Himachal Pradesh traces a Himalayan journey from wool and barter to women entrepreneurs and digital payments

What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women).

Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.

articles.title: Must balance ‘economic patriotism’ with cultural heritage: GJC on PM Modi’s call to stop gold purchases
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) argued that the gold jewellery sector contributes nearly 7-8% to the economy and supports millions of livelihoods

While welcoming Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for prioritising locally-made products and reducing gold imports, the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) has said that India must balance “economic patriotism” and its cultural traditions when it comes to gold jewellery.

It argued that the sector contributes “nearly 7-8%” to the economy and supports “millions of livelihoods”. The GJC was reacting to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s recent and repeated appeal to all Indians to stop foreign trips and weddings, to buy local, and to only buy gold if necessary.

“The Prime Minister’s appeal for economic patriotism and greater preference for Swadeshi products is timely and welcome,” Rajesh Rokde, Chairman of the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) said.

“While we fully support the Prime Minister’s call for restraint when gold is viewed purely as bullion or an investment instrument, jewellery consumption remains closely linked to culture, craftsmanship, and livelihoods,” Mr. Rokde added.
He said that gold and jewellery hold a unique place in India’s cultural heritage, particularly during festive and wedding seasons, such as the period that India will soon enter in October-December.
“The jewellery industry, contributing nearly 7-8% to the economy and supporting millions of livelihoods, is an integral part of India’s growth story,” Mr. Rokde asserted.
‘People bought less gold, prices fell’: Modi recalls year-old appeal

“As a ₹10 lakh crore industry, the Indian jewellery sector must continue to grow responsibly, with greater transparency, value creation, and alignment with national priorities — balancing economic patriotism with India’s enduring cultural traditions,” he added.

articles.title: Russian attack near Ukraine’s capital strikes apartment building, killing two and wounding four others
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Rescuers evacuated nine people, including a child, from the destroyed five-storey building in Dymer, while 11 were believed to be trapped under the rubble

A Russian attack struck an apartment building in a village near Ukraine’s capital on Sunday (November 22, 2026), killing at least two people and wounding four others, authorities said. Nearly a dozen people were feared trapped beneath the rubble.

The morning strike destroyed the five-storey building in Dymer, which is north of Kyiv. Rescuers have evacuated nine people, including a child, authorities said, while another child was hospitalised with injuries. Search and rescue teams worked to find other survivors. Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said 11 people were believed to be trapped.

“When (the explosion came), I literally flipped over in bed,” said Mykola Osadnyi, a relative of some of those trapped. “I live about 200 metres from here. Then we ran over here.” “My father-in-law … was screaming, ‘Save me, I’m burning!’” Mr. Osadnyi said.

“And now we’re just waiting again to see what happens.” Another resident, Olena Kharkavliuk, recounted that “a terrifying sound woke us up, and then there was an explosion”. “My husband and I have been waiting here since about 4 am, because my older daughter’s classmate and her mother are in there,” Ms. Kharkavliuk told AP .

Meanwhile, a rare air alert sounded in Kaliningrad, a Russian exclave near Poland and Lithuania, according to the local Governor, as claims circulated online of drone activity near a major naval base there.

The alert late on Saturday (November 21, 2026) came hours after a drone strike in the Gulf of Finland set fire to a Russian cargo ship bound for the region, a key base for Russia’s Baltic Fleet. Finnish emergency services were still working to extinguish the blaze on Sunday (November 22, 2026).

Photos and video posted online show drone activity around the city of Baltiysk, where much of the fleet is stationed, but AP could not immediately verify their authenticity. According to local media, air raid sirens were heard in Kaliningrad for the first time since Russia’s all-out invasion of Ukraine on February 24, 2022.

Governor Alexei Bezprozvannykh said “a suspicious object coming from the direction of Lithuania” triggered the alert in the Nemansky district near the Lithuanian border, about 170 km north-east of Baltiysk.
On Russian Telegram channels, posts by users saying they were Baltiysk residents described air defences working there during the night, with photos and videos of bright streaks against the night sky.

Kaliningrad authorities on Sunday (November 22, 2026) denounced as fake one photo, supposedly from Baltiysk, showing clouds of smoke rising into the night sky, telling Russian State media that it “had nothing to do with the region.” As of Sunday morning (November 22, 2026), Russian authorities reported no casualties or damage in Kaliningrad.

fullParagraphs: Research institutions need timely funding, better teaching incentives, greater autonomy, leadership control, safeguards against quid pro quo, and reduced administrative burdens

Modern science rightly prides itself on independent scrutiny, irrespective of where the scrutiniser is located. There is no reason seeking the assessment of someone outside India has to constitute colonialism. Yet this was the charge in a widely debated article by Sanjeev Sanyal, Satvik Dev, and Payal Sharma, respectively a Member, the Joint Director, and a Young Professional on the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister.

Researchers write up a study and submit it as a manuscript to a journal. Editors at the journal assess the manuscript and send it out to other experts in the field, asking if the work is worth publishing, or needs to be revised or rejected. If the journal accepts the paper, it will be published, brought to the attention of scientists worldwide, and have a permanent record of it preserved.

articles.title: Chandel district official issues advisory after spurious liquor kills 11 in Manipur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Chandel district authorities have urged the people to report suspected manufacturing, storage, sale or distribution of adulterated liquor
Manipur’s Chandel district administration on Friday (November 20, 2026) issued an advisory, urging people to report suspected manufacturing, storage, sale or distribution of adulterated liquor.
The public advisory followed the death of 11 people due to consumption of spurious liquor in the district’s Chakpikarong Sub-Division. The deaths have been reported since Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

According to a statement from the Chief Minister’s Office, 180 others are undergoing treatment at two private hospitals in Imphal. Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh visited these hospitals on Friday and took stock of the treatment being provided to the patients.

Advising the general public to exercise utmost caution, the district administration said the cause of the deaths was yet to be “medically and scientifically established”. It asked people to refrain from consuming locally brewed liquor or alcoholic beverages of doubtful origin, particularly from suspected sources in the affected areas.

“Any person experiencing vomiting, abdominal pain, headache, dizziness, blurred vision, breathing difficulty or other unusual symptoms following alcohol consumption should immediately seek medical attention at the nearest facility,” the advisory read.
It also advised people who may have consumed liquor from the same suspected source to seek medical evaluation even if they are not experiencing symptoms.

“The public is requested to report suspected manufacturing, storage, sale or distribution of adulterated liquor to the nearest police station or the concerned authorities,” the advisory further read, requesting village authorities, civil society organisations, women’s organisations and youth clubs to assist in spreading awareness.

The Manipur government partially lifted 30 years of alcohol prohibition in December 2023, although extremist groups in the State continue to target liquor businesses. Years of prohibition led to certain areas turning into local liquor dens, selling alcoholic beverages of suspect quality.
Spurious liquor has claimed lives in other northeastern States where prohibition is enforced. For instance, 23 people were killed in Nagaland’s Mokokchung and Tuensang districts about two months ago.

articles.title: PM to visit Bihar to inaugurate a six-lane bridge named after ex-CM Nitish
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: JD(U) working chief Sanjay Kumar Jha said that “the decision of CM Choudhary to name the bridge as Nitish Setu symbolises the immense affection, respect, and gratitude that Bihar people have for our leader Nitish Kumar”

On the completion of one year of NDA government rule in Bihar, Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit the Vaishali district on November 21 to inaugurate a six-lane bridge and lay the foundation stone for several other projects. PM Modi is also likely to address a public meeting after the scheduled ceremonies in the district.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to inaugurate a 9.76 km long ₹5,500 crore six-lane bridge on the River Ganga, connecting Kacchi Dargah in Patna district to Bidupur in the neighbouring Vaishali district. The government has named the bridge after former Chief Minister and ruling NDA ally Nitish Kumar as “Nitish Setu.”

The Opposition Rashtriya Janata Dal recently raised objections, claiming that the bridge was conceived in 2015 when the Mahagathbandhan (grand alliance) government was in power in the State, and the party has also demanded that the bridge be named after RJD chief Lalu Prasad.

RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav, who is also the leader of the Opposition in the State Assembly, and his parents Lalu Prasad and Rabri Devi, have been representing the flood-prone Raghopur for several terms in the Assembly and the constituency has been a bastion of the Other Backward Class “Yadav” caste for long.

“Nitish Setu will make travel between north and south Bihar smoother and faster, offering significant benefits to the people of Patna, Vaishali, and surrounding districts,” Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary said. However, RJD national working president Tejashwi Yadav took a dig at this, expressing wonder: “I’ve heard that such bridges or monuments are only named after people who are no more. I guess the BJP, by naming the bridge as Nitish Setu, has gobbled up Nitish Kumar, and he doesn’t exist for them.”

However, JD(U) working president Sanjay Kumar Jha said that “the decision of Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary to name the bridge as Nitish Setu symbolises the immense affection, respect, and gratitude that the people of Bihar have for our leader Nitish Kumar ji.”

For the first time in the state, senior BJP leader Samrat Choudhary became Chief Minister in April 2026, replacing the ruling alliance leader of JD(U), Nitish Kumar. Mr. Kumar’s son, Nishant Kumar, is the Health Minister in Mr. Choudhary’s cabinet. Following in the footsteps of his predecessor and former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar, Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary is likely to embark on his statewide tour on November 26, 2026, from the West Champaran district.

On the completion of one year of NDA government rule in Bihar, Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit the Vaishali district on November 21 to inaugurate a six-lane bridge and lay the foundation stone for several other projects. PM Modi is also likely to address a public meeting after the scheduled ceremonies in the district.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to inaugurate a 9.76 km long ₹5,500 crore six-lane bridge on the River Ganga, connecting Kacchi Dargah in Patna district to Bidupur in the neighbouring Vaishali district. The government has named the bridge after former Chief Minister and ruling NDA ally Nitish Kumar as “Nitish Setu.”

The Opposition Rashtriya Janata Dal recently raised objections, claiming that the bridge was conceived in 2015 when the Mahagathbandhan (grand alliance) government was in power in the State, and the party has also demanded that the bridge be named after RJD chief Lalu Prasad.

RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav, who is also the leader of the Opposition in the State Assembly, and his parents Lalu Prasad and Rabri Devi, have been representing the flood-prone Raghopur for several terms in the Assembly and the constituency has been a bastion of the Other Backward Class “Yadav” caste for long.

“Nitish Setu will make travel between north and south Bihar smoother and faster, offering significant benefits to the people of Patna, Vaishali, and surrounding districts,” Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary said. However, RJD national working president Tejashwi Yadav took a dig at this, expressing wonder: “I’ve heard that such bridges or monuments are only named after people who are no more. I guess the BJP, by naming the bridge as Nitish Setu, has gobbled up Nitish Kumar, and he doesn’t exist for them.”

However, JD(U) working president Sanjay Kumar Jha said that “the decision of Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary to name the bridge as Nitish Setu symbolises the immense affection, respect, and gratitude that the people of Bihar have for our leader Nitish Kumar ji.”

For the first time in the state, senior BJP leader Samrat Choudhary became Chief Minister in April 2026, replacing the ruling alliance leader of JD(U), Nitish Kumar. articles.title: West Bengal CEO office postpones SSR due to unavoidable circumstances
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The development comes ahead of pending civic elections in West Bengal. The State government is keen to hold elections to the civic bodies of Howrah and Kolkata.

The West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer’s (CEO) office announced on Friday (November 20, 2026) the postponement of the Special Summary Revision (SSR) of the Photo Electoral Roll, 2027, which was scheduled to commence on November 23. The CEO’s office, in a statement, added that the decision has been taken due to “unavoidable circumstances.” The revised schedule for the exercise will be intimated subsequently, the statement said.
Editorial | Incomplete remedies: On Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls

“The upcoming programme of Special Summary Revision of Photo Electoral Roll, which was scheduled from 23 November 2026 onwards, is hereby postponed due to some unavoidable circumstances,” the press statement said. As per the SSR schedule announced in the State, the publication of final electoral rolls is scheduled for January 2027.

The SSR, an annual exercise, usually seeks to enrol eligible voters—particularly young and first-time electors—and facilitate advance applications from those who will become eligible on April 1, July 1, and October 1, 2027. However, it had not been carried out after the SIR was launched last year.

The development comes ahead of pending civic elections in West Bengal. The state government is keen to hold elections to the civic bodies of Howrah and Kolkata. The Calcutta High Court had stayed elections to the Kolkata Municipal Corporation on the grounds that the challenge to the delimitation of wards of the civic body should be addressed by the Court before elections are declared.

The SSR will not come to the aid of the 38 lakh electors whose fate is pending before SIR tribunals after their names were removed from the voter list. According to an affidavit filed by the ECI in September earlier this year, of the 27 lakh electors who were excluded from the electoral rolls on the ground of “logical discrepancies,” 22 lakh voters have filed appeals before the tribunal challenging their exclusion. The EC’s affidavit also added that 16.10 lakh appeals have been filed against inclusions during SIR. This puts the total number of appeals of 38 lakh electors pending before the SIR tribunals.

articles.title: Congress proposes four-point formula for delimitation, says INDIA bloc on board
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Party proposes retaining 543 Lok Sabha seats, existing State-wise distribution and a 25-year freeze, with one-third reservation for women

The Congress party on Friday said it favoured resolving the issue of delimitation through consultations with all political parties, but accused the government of making no effort to engage the Opposition on the matter.

Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said the party’s position was guided by a four-point formula: retaining the existing strength of 543 seats in the Lok Sabha; maintaining the present State-wise distribution of seats; reserving one-third (182) of the existing seats for women; and imposing a 25-year freeze on all three arrangements.

Mr. Ramesh said the need for an early consensus on the issue had become more pressing in view of of the fact that Article 82 of the Constitution will come into force and delimitation would be held once the results of the ongoing Census exercise are out early next year.
This could be unfavourable to some southern states – which have made progress in population control – and hence not feasible, he added.
Mr. Ramesh said the Congress was not opposed to delimitation as such, but believed that the exercise should not place any State at a disadvantage.

The Congress leader claimed that all parties in the INDIA bloc, including the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and the Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar), were on the same page on the four-point formula.
The DMK, he said, was also party to a resolution opposing any change in the number of Lok Sabha seats and seeking safeguards to ensure that Tamil Nadu was not disadvantaged by delimitation.
The Congress leader said seeking consultation was necessary because the government had not initiated any meaningful engagement with the Opposition.
He claimed that as per his information, the government has not shared a concrete proposal on delimitation even with constituents of the National Democratic Alliance.
The Congress wanted the matter to be discussed with all political parties and stakeholders to arrive at a consensus, Mr. Ramesh added.

Party proposes retaining 543 Lok Sabha seats, existing State-wise distribution and a 25-year freeze, with one-third reservation for women

The Congress party on Friday said it favoured resolving the issue of delimitation through consultations with all political parties, but accused the government of making no effort to engage the Opposition on the matter.

Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said the party’s position was guided by a four-point formula: retaining the existing strength of 543 seats in the Lok Sabha; maintaining the present State-wise distribution of seats; reserving one-third (182) of the existing seats for women; and imposing a 25-year freeze on all three arrangements.

Mr. Ramesh said the need for an early consensus on the issue had become more pressing in view of of the fact that Article 82 of the Constitution will come into force and delimitation would be held once the results of the ongoing Census exercise are out early next year.

This could be unfavourable to some southern states – which have made progress in population control – and hence not feasible, he added.

Mr. Ramesh said the Congress was not opposed to delimitation as such, but believed that the exercise should not place any State at a disadvantage.

The Congress leader claimed that all parties in the INDIA bloc, including the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and the Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar), were on the same page on the four-point formula.

The DMK, he said, was also party to a resolution opposing any change in the number of Lok Sabha seats and seeking safeguards to ensure that Tamil Nadu was not disadvantaged by delimitation.

The Congress leader said seeking consultation was necessary because the government had not initiated any meaningful engagement with the Opposition.

He claimed that as per his information, the government has not shared a concrete proposal on delimitation even with constituents of the National Democratic Alliance.

The Congress wanted the matter to be discussed with all political parties and stakeholders to arrive at a consensus, Mr. Ramesh added.

articles.title: Patna High Court quashes dismissal of teachers and staff of Sanskrit Colleges
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The court has directed the Bihar Education Department to release the grant-in-aid to the university within three months.

Principals, teachers, and non-teaching staff of various Sanskrit colleges affiliated with Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University (KSDSU) received relief from the Patna High Court on Friday (November 20, 2026).

A single-judge bench presided over by Justice Kumar Manish, while hearing 12 connected petitions (lead case: Birendra Prasad Thakur v. State of Bihar, CWJC No. 13475/2022), quashed all dismissal orders issued by the Director of Higher Education and the university.

The petitioners were appointed between 2008 and 2015 in various affiliated and “deficit grant-in-aid” Sanskrit colleges located in Supaul, West Champaran, East Champaran, Patna, Saran, and Jehanabad, following due process involving public advertisements and selection committees.

Despite the university’s Syndicate confirming their services, the Director of Higher Education cited the absence of prior approval from the State Government, as required under Section 35(2) of the Bihar State Universities Act, 1976, and rejected these appointments on April 21, 2022, and November 2, 2022. Subsequently, the university issued directives to terminate their services.

In its judgment, the High Court cited the ruling of a Full Bench in Braj Kishore Singh v. State of Bihar (1997). The Court clarified that, when posts have already been created and sanctioned (under an established ‘staffing pattern’) pursuant to the State Government’s resolution dated October 18, 1976, separate ‘prior approval’ from the government is not mandatory for appointments to those posts made through a valid selection process.
“Dismissing an employee on technical grounds after more than a decade of service constitutes a violation of Articles 14, 16, and 21 of the Constitution,” the court observed.
Expressing concern over the proliferation of unnecessary litigation in cases of a similar nature, the court cited Clause 4(C)(1) of the Bihar State Litigation Policy, 2011.
The court directed that a copy of the order be sent to the Chief Secretary and the Advocate General. The court emphasised that such similar cases should be resolved at the departmental level.

Declaring the service of all the petitioners to be valid, the court has directed the Bihar Education Department to release the grant-in-aid to the university within three months of receiving a copy of the order.
“This is to ensure that the petitioners receive their regular current salaries, as well as all outstanding salary arrears accrued from the date of their initial appointment,” the court said.

articles.title: Woman delivers triplets after non-ART treatment at Telangana govt. hospital; premature babies discharged after NICU care
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: After a nine-year wait and unsuccessful fertility treatment at private hospitals, a couple welcomed triplet boys following treatment at Gandhi Hospital’s IVF Centre. The premature babies, who weighed between 1.4 kg and 1.5 kg at birth, spent over a month in the hospital’s Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU). They were discharged along with their 32-year-old mother after responding well to treatment.
Avanthi enrolled at Gandhi Hospital’s IVF Centre in January this year. Doctors opted for ovulation induction, a non-assisted reproductive treatment, and she conceived in the second cycle.

After scans revealed a triplet pregnancy and a short cervix, doctors performed a McDonald’s cervical cerclage at 14 weeks. However, her water broke prematurely at 32 weeks, prompting doctors to deliver the babies on October 7. The newborns were admitted to the NICU, where they received treatment and close monitoring for over a month before being discharged with their mother.

Director of Medical Education Vanii appreciated the efforts of the team, including head of the Department of Gynaecology Shobha, IVF specialists Krishnaveni and Fathima Rafi, embryologist Shiva Krishna, lab technician Ashok and counsellor Kavitha.

IVF specialist Dr Krishnaveni said that they opted ovulation induction as a first line of treatment, which is not a In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) method. “We conduct evaluations to know if non-IVF methods can be used as first line of treatment to avoid burden on couples who are already in distress,” she said. Currently, over 500 couples have rolled for treatments at the government hospitals IVF centre.

fullParagraphs: First proposed by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and is widely regarded as the most important open question in pure mathematics

A mathematician at AI company Anthropic said Friday (November 20, 2026) that he had used the firm’s Claude chatbot to prove the Riemann Hypothesis, a problem that has eluded mathematicians for more than 160 years.

The claim has not been independently verified, and the proof has not yet been reviewed by outside experts.

First proposed by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and is widely regarded as the most important open question in pure mathematics.

Under the institute’s rules, a solution must be published in a peer-reviewed journal and withstand two years of scrutiny.

articles.title: Three to tango: On Trump, Xi, Putin trilateral summit
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: U.S., China, Russia must draw up a roadmap for talks on nuclear weapons

The first trilateral summit between the Presidents of China, the U.S. and Russia , held in Shenzhen on November 19, reflected both the changing global order and the leaders’ shared desire to remain engaged with one another in an increasingly unpredictable world. For U.S. President Donald Trump, the summit was a platform where he could push for joint talks between the world’s three largest nuclear powers on reducing nuclear warheads. After the New START treaty between the U.S. and Russia expired in February 2026, Moscow had signalled that it was ready for talks, but Mr. Trump wanted to involve China as well. For President Xi Jinping, the summit reinforced China’s position as a peer competitor to the U.S. While Russia seeks to deepen partnership with China, the U.S. is looking to build strategic stability. And for Russian President Vladimir Putin, whom the West sought to isolate after he launched the invasion of Ukraine, the summit offered a seat at the high table. The decision to start trilateral talks on nuclear arms and the joint declaration, which stated that ‘a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought’, are steps in the right direction. But much will depend on what follows.

Many had compared the meet to the 1945 Yalta Conference, when Russian leader Joseph Stalin, U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill met to discuss the future of post-War Europe. But Shenzhen was not a summit of the victors of a major war. This was more about three great powers setting terms of engagement in a changing world. The summit failed to achieve any breakthrough on any of the issues on the agenda — nuclear arms reduction, non-proliferation or the Ukraine war — or even offer a road map for the future. Moreover, it is not clear if the Shenzhen spirit could be sustained in the medium to long-term as another President in the U.S. could take a very different approach towards Russia and China. The three leaders have called for reform of the UN. While it is a welcome move, any attempt to reform the international system and institutions must also involve other powers, particularly rising middle powers such as India, South Africa and Brazil. But the Shenzhen framework could bring greater stability and predictability to great-power relations. This is important given that two of the Big Three are currently waging two separate wars. The leaders should draw up a clear road map for nuclear talks and other key issues outlined in the Shenzhen declaration, with realistic and achievable objectives. Otherwise, the summit would amount to little more than another diplomatic photo-op.

articles.title: Koti Deepotsavam emerges as grand confluence of Shaiva, Vaishnava traditions in Telangana
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Bringing together revered spiritual heads, sacred rituals and devotees from across the State, the annual celebration offers a rare opportunity to experience diverse Hindu traditions at one venue, with the illumination of a crore earthen lamps forming its grand spectacle

A confluence of Shaiva and Vaishnava traditions, a congregation of revered spiritual heads from across the country and the illumination of a crore lamps have made Koti Deepotsavam one of Telangana’s biggest religious celebrations outside temple premises.

Held every year in Kartika month, the event draws thousands of devotees from different parts of the State, not merely to witness the ceremonies but also to participate in an array of rituals that are otherwise not easily accessible to the common devotee.
Koti Deepotsavam offers devotees an opportunity to perform abhishekams, offer bilva leaves to Shiva Lingams, worship the Goddess and participate in special pujas and other ceremonies.
The presence of Jagadgurus and heads of prominent peethams adds another dimension, enabling devotees to seek their blessings and have their darshan, an opportunity that many may seldom get otherwise.

Over the past 13 years, Koti Deepotsavam has given a distinctive identity to the month of Kartika and to Telangana. The initiative began in 2012 as a Laksha Deepotsavam, or the lighting of one lakh lamps, and the following year evolved into Koti Deepotsavam, involving a crore lamps. The idea was conceived by Narendra Chowdary and his wife Ramadevi, and daughter Rachana, who run Bhakti TV.

The genesis of the initiative lay in a visit by Sringeri Dakshinamnaya Peetham Jagadguru Sri Bharati Tirtha Mahaswami to Hyderabad during his Vijaya Yatra in 2012, when Kartika Deepotsavam was combined with the darshan of the Jagadguru for the Guru Vandanam.

The first edition was organised at NTR Stadium, where a specially constructed stage depicting the grandeur of Kailasa provided the setting for the celebrations. The Sringeri Jagadguru performed Deeparadhana and blessed the devotees.

By 2013, the Laksha Deepotsavam had grown into Koti Deepotsavam. What began as a single religious gathering gradually developed into an elaborate annual celebration, incorporating several traditions, rituals and cultural presentations.
“The objective has been to recreate the experience of visiting important pilgrimage centres by bringing the deities and their traditions together at one venue,” says Mr. Narendra Chowdary.

A distinctive feature is the presence of utsava murtis representing important temples and pilgrimage centres. Deities associated with the 12 Jyotirlingas, Pancha Bhuta Lingas, 18 Shakti Peethas and Divya Desams of the Sri Vaishnava tradition are brought to the venue and worshipped. Shaiva centres such as Ujjain, Arunachalam, Vemulawada and Kaleshwaram find representation alongside Vaishnava shrines such as Yadadri and Srirangam, and Shakti Peethas including Alampur, Kanchi and Varanasi.

fullParagraphs: Scientists indicate that the ongoing strong El Niño could persist until March 2027, followed by neutral conditions and a possible transition to La Niña during the Southwest Monsoon. They are also monitoring widespread marine heatwaves across the Indian Ocean

While the powerful El Niño continues to strengthen over the Pacific Ocean, scientists are beginning to see signs that its cooler counterpart, La Niña, could emerge by the time the Southwest Monsoon arrives in 2027.

Scientists at the Hyderabad-based Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS) say the ongoing El Niño is likely to remain dominant until March next year. But, climate models indicate a gradual transition to neutral conditions thereafter, followed by increasing chances of La Niña development during the 2027 Southwest monsoon season.

articles.title: India says no change in its position on Indus Water Treaty as Pakistan minister attends SCO forum in Delhi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: India suspended the treaty in 2025 as one of the punitive measures against Pakistan after the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack last year that claimed 26 lives

India's position on the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) is "very clear" and there has been "absolutely no change" in it, the Ministry of External Affairs said on Friday (November 20, 2026), amid a visit by Pakistan Minister Musadik Malik to attend the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in Delhi.

Mr. Malik, who arrived here in the early hours of Friday (November 20, 2026), attended the opening day of the three-day forum in the evening. The event, being hosted by India at the historic Purana Quila, was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
India had announced on October 28 that invitations had been extended to all SCO members, including Pakistan, in keeping with established practice.
It was perhaps the first time New Delhi had invited a Pakistani minister to attend an event in India since the May 7-10 military hostilities last year following Operation Sindoor.
Pakistan had announced on November 14 that its Climate Change Minister Malik would participate in the forum.
"As far as IWT is concerned, we have made our position very clear, and that is where it remains. There is absolutely no change," Mr. Jaiswal said.
India suspended the treaty in 2025 as one of the punitive measures against Pakistan after the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack last year that claimed 26 lives.
Mr. Malik's participation in the forum is being seen by some experts as an opportunity in a multilateral framework that may help improve ties between the two neighbours.

Interacting with reporters on the sidelines of the forum, Mr. Malik, when asked about the role of culture in fostering better ties between India and Pakistan, said, "Culture has a very key role to play".

Hours before the inauguration, the MEA on Friday (November 20, 2026) said the forum was a "multilateral event within the SCO framework", for which invitations had been extended to all members of the grouping, including Pakistan.

articles.title: Magnitude 6.9 earthquake shakes Peru’s Andes, with no damage or casualties immediately reported
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Peru's Geophysical Institute said no damage or casualties had been reported. The earthquake was felt in the Peruvian capital, prompting residents to rush into the streets
A magnitude 6.9 earthquake shook the Andes in central Peru on Friday (November 20, 2026) with no immediate reports of damage or casualties.

The U.S. Geological Survey said the earthquake struck at 7:09 pm local time (0900 GMT Saturday). Its epicentre was in the Andes, 34 kilometres (21 miles) north of Junin, at a depth of 108 kilometres (67 miles).
Peru's Geophysical Institute said no damage or casualties had been reported. The earthquake was felt in the Peruvian capital, prompting residents to rush into the streets.
Peru lies along the "Ring of Fire", a 40,000-kilometre (25,000-mile) arc of volcanoes and fault lines around the Pacific Basin, where most of the world's earthquakes occur.

In August, a 6.7 magnitude earthquake in the Peruvian Andes left two people injured and damaged several homes, health centres and schools, while in July, a 5.5-magnitude quake in the Junín region resulted in six deaths and 30 injuries.

articles.title: In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Attappady’s recurring infant deaths this year point to a crisis that goes beyond malnutrition and access to timely healthcare. Poverty, land alienation, and the erosion of traditional food systems, are taking a toll on maternal and child health in this predominantly tribal region of Keralam

Between the pages of a logbook recording Dakshina’s treatment are ₹100, ₹50, ₹20, and ₹10 notes. Dakshina’s mother, Minnal Rani, had filed them away for her daughter’s medical expenses. The child is gone, but the money remains untouched. “We will never spend it,” she says, fighting back tears.

Dakshina was five months old when doctors detected a hole in her heart. Born on June 13, 2025, she was taken to many hospitals, including one in Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam’s capital. With surgery ruled out, she was eventually referred to a cooperative hospital at Perinthalmanna, in Malappuram district, a two-and-a-half-hour drive away from home. She died here, on April 13, 2026.
Rani and her husband Chandra Sekhar say the hospital refused to release their daughter’s body until they paid a bill of ₹10,000. They managed to raise the money with the help of a ward councillor.
“We buried her under that tree,” says Rani, pointing to a coconut tree near their house at Vechapathi hamlet in Sholayur panchayat of Attappadi, Palakkad district.

Dakshina’s death is among a series of 10 infant deaths reported this year from Attappadi, a predominantly tribal settlement. There have been four back-to-back deaths in October. Of the 10 infant deaths, six involved congenital anomalies, with heart defects among the commonly reported conditions. An expert committee of doctors and researchers is examining the deaths.

In a step towards promoting industrial development and attracting investment in Bihar, Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) were signed for six energy projects on Friday (November 20, 2026) during the Entrepreneurs’ Interaction and MoU Exchange Ceremony organised under Bihar Business Connect–2026. These projects envisage a total investment of ₹1,72,885 crore in the state’s energy sector.

The projects have two nuclear power plants and four pumped storage projects. The two nuclear power plants will be established in Banka and Siwan districts, while the four pumped storage projects will be developed in Nawada, Jamui and Aurangabad districts.

Among the total investment proposals worth ₹2.25 lakh crore received by the Energy and Industries Departments under Bihar Business Connect, the agreements for these six energy projects will strengthen the State’s power generation and energy storage capacity. Once implemented, these projects will help meet Bihar’s future electricity requirements, enhance energy security and accelerate industrial growth.
Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit (IAS) and Energy Secretary-cum-Chairman and Managing Director of Bihar State Power Holding Company Limited (BSPHCL) Ajay Yadav (IAS).
Vishal Raj (IAS), Managing Director of Bihar State Power Generation Company Limited, exchanged the MoUs with representatives of various companies.

The participating representatives included Sumit Verma, Head – Business Development and Strategy, Adani Group, Krishna Tungaturthi, Chief Operation Officer (COO) - Pumped Storage- Greenko Group, Jigish Mehta, Director, Torrent Power; S. He further said that the State government is providing 125 units of free electricity every month to 1.92 crore domestic consumers. In addition, rooftop solar installations are being encouraged through the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana and other solar energy schemes.

articles.title: Mahipalpur flyover a daily traffic bottleneck for half a million Delhi-Gurugram commuters
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Multiple merging points, U-turns and downstream bottlenecks contribute to persistent jams on NH-48; proposed decongestion measures include regulating vehicle entry and enforcing lane discipline

A long line of red tail-lights stretches along the Mahipalpur flyover on National Highway-48 every day as commuters make their way between home and work. With at least half a million commuters using the flyover daily, according to Delhi Traffic Police estimates, the corridor connecting central Delhi with Gurugram has become a persistent traffic bottleneck. Vehicles begin slowing down even before reaching the flyover, with queues frequently stretching beyond it.
Police sources attributed the congestion to multiple traffic streams converging at Telco Cut and Radisson, frequent merging and lane changes, and bottlenecks on the roads beyond the flyover.

Gajender Rawat, a private-sector employee who travels from his residence in Paschim Vihar to his workplace in Gurugram, said he spends at least 30-40 minutes crossing the flyover every day — roughly the time his entire home-to-work journey would take in the absence of traffic.

“Vehicles begin slowing down almost as soon as we enter the flyover while travelling from Delhi towards Gurugram, with congestion stretching towards the Gurugram side. It is the same story on the way back, especially if you travel during peak office hours,” Gajender Rawat said. On Wednesday, he took over 1.5 hours to cross the stretch during peak hours.
For some commuters, avoiding the corridor altogether has become the only practical solution.
Denis Gupta, another private-sector employee who travels daily from Rohini to Gurugram, said he takes the Urban Extension Road (UER), despite the longer distance and toll charges.

“I stopped using that route altogether because of the long traffic jams. I now take the UER, which is a longer route and takes around an hour, and have to pay toll for it. But I’d rather pay and drive longer than get stuck in a traffic jam. Ultimately, it takes longer on the shorter route because of the jam,” he said.

Commuters have also repeatedly flagged the problem on social media, describing the flyover as a “permanent choke point” and raising concerns over traffic management and passenger pick-ups and drop-offs along the stretch.

“Over the last five-six months, there has been a permanent traffic jam at Mahipalpur flyover. We do not see police personnel at major choke points. Shiv Murti has become a bus stand, with long-distance buses stopping to pick up passengers. Cabs drop passengers near the hotel at Mahipalpur flyover,” a commuter wrote on X, sharing a Google Maps screenshot showing a travel time of 1 hour and 43 minutes for 36 km.

A proposed decongestion plan prepared by the traffic police focuses on regulating the volume of vehicles entering the flyover rather than merely increasing signal timings. Traffic police official said the plan recommends controlled entry from feeder roads such as Telco Cut and Radisson, channelising merging and U-turn movements, and enforcing lane discipline to prevent sudden lane changes on the flyover.

articles.title: U.S. court dispatches summonses to Doval, Goel in Pannun case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Indian Code of Civil Procedure permits summonses issued by foreign civil courts designated by notification of the Central Government of India to be transmitted to Indian courts and served as though issued by those courts

A U.S. court has dispatched summonses to National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and former Research and Analysis Wing Director Samant Goel in connection with a case involving Khalistani separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun.
Pannun is wanted by Indian probe agencies on various terror charges.

The clerk of the Southern District Court of New York said that the summonses were sent through FedEx to the Patiala House Court, Tis Hazari Court, and the Dwarka District Court in New Delhi on Friday (November 20, 2026).
On November 13, the Southern District Court of New York ordered that summonses be issued to Mr. Doval and Mr. Goel, citing the Hague Convention.

“The Court respectfully requests the assistance of receiving Indian courts in effecting service of process upon the defendants in this civil action pending before this court,” read an order by Judge Katherine Polk Failla.
Judge Failla cited the Hague Conventions and relevant sections of the Indian Code of Civil Procedure to state that foreign courts can serve summonses on Mr. Doval and Mr. Goel through Indian courts.

The Indian Code of Civil Procedure permits summonses issued by foreign civil courts designated by notification of the Central Government of India to be transmitted to Indian courts and served as though issued by those courts.

The order states that standard service through India's central authority under the Hague Convention was attempted but rejected. The Court then authorised alternative service under Article 19 of the Hague Convention and India's Code of Civil Procedure.
Pannun, legal counsel for the banned organisation Sikhs for Justice (SFJ), has filed the civil lawsuit seeking damages over an alleged attempt on his life.
He has accused Mr. Doval of orchestrating a plot involving India's foreign intelligence agency to assassinate him.

The decision was taken at a meeting of the identification committee held at the residence of Minister Ponnam Prabhakar at the Ministers’ Quarters on Saturday (November 21, 2026). The meeting was chaired by committee chairman K. Keshava Rao and attended by Mr. Ponnam Prabhakar, MLC Professor Kodandaram, former MLC Ramulu Naik, Mothe Shobhan Reddy and Shyam Mohan.
The committee reviewed the progress made so far in identifying those who had participated in the Telangana movement and discussed the measures required to take the process forward.
It noted that consultations had already been held with activists from various universities, artists and representatives of different sections of society as part of the exercise.

A major part of the meeting was devoted to reviewing the status of the proposed website through which the identification process would be facilitated. Members discussed the timeline for its launch and felt that the website should be made operational at the earliest to ensure that the recognition exercise could proceed smoothly. The committee reiterated its commitment to completing the identification process at the earliest.

articles.title: Telangana issues guidelines for ₹5 lakh Indiramma family life insurance scheme; permits only one application per ration card
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Telangana government will undertake a month-long enrolment drive through special camps at the gram panchayat level in rural areas and designated wards in urban areas

The Telangana government has issued guidelines for enrolment under the Indiramma Kutumba Jeevitha Bima Padhakam (IKJBP), which provides life insurance coverage of ₹5 lakh to one member of each eligible household, following the launch of the scheme by Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy in Siddipet on Thursday (November 19, 2026).

The Planning Department has stipulated that only one person per family, ordinarily the earning member identified by the household, can be enrolled under the scheme. The government has lined the scheme with the ration card and the ration card number will serve as the application number. Only one application permitted per ration card and enrolment will be based on ration cards issued in Telangana. Families holding ration cards issued in another district of the State can register at their nearest camp, while verification will be carried out by officials in their home district.

The scheme is intended to provide financial security to vulnerable families by extending an insurance benefit of ₹5 lakh to the nominee or nominees in the event of the insured member’s death. The government has clarified that all existing State-sponsored insurance schemes will continue but will be brought under the IKJBP umbrella.
According to the guidelines, persons aged between 18 and 59 years at the time of enrolment are eligible for coverage.

The government will undertake a month-long enrolment drive through special camps at the gram panchayat level in rural areas and designated wards in urban areas. Additional camps will be organised wherever necessary, with special arrangements for elderly persons, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable sections.

Applicants must provide their Aadhaar details, ration card, wherever available, and mobile phone number. Households with pending ration card e-KYC must complete the process at their designated Public Distribution System (PDS) shops.

The guidelines also allow the insured member to nominate more than one person and specify the proportion of the insurance amount payable to each nominee. The shares must be expressed in whole percentages and must not exceed 100% in total.

To address registration-related difficulties, the government has directed officials to establish help desks at enrolment camps. Discrepancies in records, missing information and other exceptional cases must be documented and referred to the appropriate authorities for resolution.

articles.title: Adani Defence fires four anti-tank missiles in Pokhran Test Range
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The missile is capable of engaging armour at up to 8 km, twice the approximately 4 km range of the land-based anti-tank missile

Adani Defence & Aerospace, the Adani Group's flagship defence and aerospace company, successfully demonstrated Bagheera AT1, a vehicle-mounted anti-tank guided missile (ATGM) system, at the Pokhran Field Firing Ranges in Rajasthan.

"The programme validated day and night engagements, a two-missile tandem firing along a single beam against a target representing an armoured vehicle, and an aerial-target engagement at an extended range. It was followed by a static display of the complete system," the company said in a statement.
The No Cost No Commitment (NCNC) demonstration at Pokhran on November 20 was witnessed by senior representatives of the Indian Army, Department of Military Affairs and Ministry of Defence (MoD).

"Bagheera AT1 is the outcome of 18 months of design and development, during which Adani Defence customised the missile system for Indian terrain, climate and operational requirements. The result is a complete combat system comprising the missile, automated launcher, day and night sights, mounted on an Adani Defence- designed 4x4 high-mobility armoured vehicle," it said.

The missile is capable of engaging armour at up to 8 km, twice the approximately 4 km range of the land-based anti-tank missile. It rides a laser beam rather than relying on a radio link, making it highly resistant to electronic jamming on a battlefield increasingly shaped by drones and electronic warfare.

The company said two missiles can be fired in quick succession along the same beam at a single target. "The first engages the tank's Active Protection System (APS), while the second is designed to penetrate its defences."

Four ready-to-fire missiles on the automated launcher and 8 reloads onboard, providing a total capacity of 12 missiles per vehicle. Also, integrated day television and thermal-imaging sights with automated target tracking. The crew engages from cover and relocates quickly to reduce exposure to enemy fire.
"The system can also engage aerial targets at extended range," the statement said.
India's requirement for modern anti-tank guided missiles remains substantial, with reported gaps in the ATGM inventory underscoring the need for continued modernisation.
The in-service backbone remains second-generation Milan-2T and Konkurs-M, with Spike missiles subsequently inducted to address immediate operational requirements.

articles.title: Karnataka government seeks action against Power TV over sting operations
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The direction follows a complaint submitted by C.B. Suresh Babu, leader of the Karnataka Janata Dal (Secular) Legislature Party, to the Governor on November 3, seeking action against the private television channel for allegedly attempting to lure ministers and legislators with monetary inducements to record sting operations

The Karnataka government has directed the Director General and Inspector General of Police (DG & IGP) to examine allegations of blackmail, extortion and entrapment levelled against Power TV chief Rakesh Shetty and employees involved in the channel’s sting operations targeting elected representatives.

The direction follows a complaint submitted by C.B. Suresh Babu, leader of the Karnataka Janata Dal (Secular) Legislature Party, to the Governor on November 3, seeking action against the private television channel for allegedly attempting to lure ministers and legislators with monetary inducements to record sting operations.

In a communication dated November 20, the Home Department’s Under Secretary (Crimes), S. Ambika, forwarded the complaint and its enclosures to the Director General and Inspector General of Police, asking the police chief to examine the allegations in accordance with the law, take necessary action and submit a detailed action-taken report to the government.

According to Mr. Suresh Babu’s complaint, the channel allegedly devised a fictitious government scheme involving the installation of optical fibre cable (OFC) in March 2023 and approached nearly 33 legislators under the banner of its programme “Power Bete.” The complaint alleges that ministers and MLAs were offered money to facilitate the implementation of the purported scheme and were subsequently portrayed in a negative light through the sting operation.

The complaint also refers to a recent sting operation involving Hassan MLA Swaroop Prakash. It alleges that the channel’s team approached his office claiming that funds under the Scheduled Caste Sub-Plan (SCSP), Tribal Sub-Plan (TSP) and Minority Welfare Department schemes could be sanctioned for his constituency in return for a five per cent commission.

Mr. Suresh Babu has alleged that the channel’s team offered and handed over money to the MLA, recorded the interaction and subsequently telecast the footage. He has claimed that the MLA did not demand money or negotiate any financial transaction and was instead induced into the situation by the sting operation team.

The representation argues that the alleged use of fictitious schemes and monetary inducements amounted to entrapment rather than a genuine exercise to expose corruption. It also raises concerns over violation of the privacy and dignity of elected representatives and misuse of the freedom of the press.

The complaint names several serving and former ministers and legislators who were allegedly targeted in the 2023 sting operation and refers to other opposition legislators, including Swaroop Prakash, in connection with the 2026 operation.

Meanwhile, a senior police official said the government’s communication had been forwarded to the Chief Commissioner of Police (CCP) for further action. The Cyber Crime wing of the Central Crime Branch (CCB) was already investigating the case, the official said.

articles.title: Infra push and low base effect pushes core sector growth to series-high of 10.9% in October 2026
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: While the coal and electricity sectors saw growth shoot up, a large part of this was due to a statistical effect rather than growth in actual output. On the other hand, fuel-related sectors contracted again

Growth in the core industrial sectors of the economy climbed to a series-high of 10.9% in October 2026, driven by a surge in electricity generation, and coal, cement, and iron ore production, and a low base effect, official data released on Friday (November 20, 2026) showed.

Data released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry on the Index of Core Industries shows that growth in October surpassed the 8.2% in September, the previous series high. The new index, released this year with a base year of 2022-23, has data that goes back only up to April 2024.
However, the data also shows that the strong growth figure in October was also likely aided by the fact that the index grew a relatively poor 0.8% in October last year.

“While core output surged by 10.9% in October 2026, the fastest pace in the new series, this was supported by a low base related to the shift in the festive calendar, with output having expanded by a marginal 0.8% in the year ago month,” Aditi Nayar, chief economist at ICRA said.

“While the growth print for October 2026 signals a strong start for the third quarter of FY2027, this is largely optical,” Ms. Nayar added. “The average performance for October-November 2026 would provide a better assessment, as this would adjust for festive base effects.”

Within the index, the coal sector saw growth accelerating to 23.05% in October 2026, far faster than the 10.7% registered in September. October’s performance, however, is likely also due to low base effect, since the sector contracted 8.4% in October last year.

The growth in the index, however, is in line with what the industry itself has reported. Coal India, the country’s largest coal company, reported that production increased about 19% to 67.2 million tonnes (MT) in October.

A major reason for the growth in coal production was likely demand from the power sector, which saw electricity generation jump by 21.6% in October 2026, up from 12.6% in the previous month. However, this sector too could have benefited from a low base effect, since it contracted nearly 7% in October 2025.
Within the index, the infrastructure-related sectors were the only ones that grew strongly without the aid of a statistical low base effect.

The iron ore sector, for example, grew at a three-month high of 23.4% in October 2026, compared to 18.4% in September and 8.7% in October last year. One of the factors driving this strong growth was that steel production grew at 7.3% in October, the fastest rate in seven months.

articles.title: European Union proposes tax on Big Tech to boost budget
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: European Council president Antonio Costa unveiled a new spending proposal that slashes by 204 billion euros a plan initially put forward by the European Commission

The European Union (EU) put forward plans to tax the world's biggest digital companies to fund its next budget on Saturday (November 21, 2026), as it seeks to bridge divisions among member states over the bloc's long-term funding.

European Council president Antonio Costa unveiled a new spending proposal that slashes by 204 billion euros ($224 billion) a plan initially put forward by the European Commission, which some countries had slammed as too onerous.
"I believe this proposal can bring us closer to a final agreement," Mr. Costa told a press conference in Brussels.

EU countries have been squabbling over the size of the next budget, with Germany leading calls for major cuts after the Commission last year proposed a two-trillion-euro budget for the 2028-2034 period.
Berlin criticised a revised proposal published last month that suggested slashing the bloc's future seven-year budget by 140 billion euros.
Mr. Costa, who represents the EU's 27 states, is seeking to reach a deal by the end of the year balancing contributions from member states with new sources of revenue for the bloc.

Among these could be a tax on digital firms that the draft Mr. Costa presented on Saturday says will concern companies with an annual turnover for digital activities of at least 50 million euros in the EU as well as a global turnover of more than 750 million euros.

articles.title: Iran says allies China, Russia oppose change in nuclear doctrine
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Iran has barred the International Atomic Energy Agency from inspecting its nuclear sites, citing security concerns and blaming the agency for failing to condemn U.S. and Israeli attacks on its nuclear facilities
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said China and Russia oppose a change in Tehran’s nuclear doctrine, amid domestic calls for a shift, state media reported.
In an interview published on Saturday (November 21, 2026), Mr. Araghchi told the state-run Iran Daily newspaper that the issue was “broad, serious” and had its own “supporters and opponents”.
“Russia and China are also opposed” to a change in Iran’s doctrine, he added. Both countries have strategic cooperation agreements with Iran.
“What matters is that, up to this point, our doctrine has not changed, and our official positions remain the same as before,” Mr. Araghchi said.

Debate over changing Iran’s nuclear doctrine has resurfaced in the country’s political circles, particularly among hardliners, following wars with Israel and the United States that saw Iranian nuclear facilities come under heavy attack.
Some advocates of a shift argue that it would pave the way for Tehran to develop a nuclear weapon as a deterrent.

Iran has barred the International Atomic Energy Agency from inspecting its nuclear sites, citing security concerns and blaming the agency for failing to condemn U.S. and Israeli attacks on its nuclear facilities.
Last week, the UN nuclear watchdog urged Iran to take “incremental steps” to allow inspectors to return to key facilities, saying such access was “critical”.

Iranian officials continue to cite a fatwa, or religious decree, issued by former supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei that prohibited the development of weapons of mass destruction, including nuclear weapons.

“There are those who believe the country’s nuclear doctrine should be maintained in its current form, and others who speak of the need to change it. Both sides have their own arguments and rationale,” Mr. Araghchi said.

articles.title: Iran-U.S. negotiations stalled over uranium enrichment dispute, mediators warn of renewed conflict, says reports
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The diplomatic deadlock comes amid continuing tensions between Washington and Tehran, with both countries yet to reach an understanding on the future of Iran's nuclear programme

Negotiations between the United States and Iran have stalled over disagreements concerning Tehran's enriched uranium stockpile , with mediators warning that they cannot guarantee a return to military escalation in West Asia.

Washington is insisting on a clear roadmap and written guarantees from Iran that it will eliminate its enriched uranium stockpile and refrain from resuming uranium enrichment in the future, Al Arabiya English reported, citing a senior source. However, both sides have maintained firm positions on the issue despite several proposals put forward by mediators to bridge their differences, the report said.

The diplomatic deadlock comes amid continuing tensions between Washington and Tehran, with both countries yet to reach an understanding on the future of Iran's nuclear programme. Earlier, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran would not accept an agreement with Washington merely to end the current diplomatic impasse, insisting that any settlement must protect Iran's national interests and provide assurances against another military confrontation.

In an interview with an Iranian state-run newspaper, as reported by Al Jazeera , Mr. Araghchi said Iran was seeking a "good, honourable and lasting agreement" rather than remaining in a situation of "neither war nor peace". Questioning the durability of any potential understanding with Washington, he said, "What is the point of reaching an agreement today if it is violated two months later and war resumes?" Mr. Araghchi recalled that fighting had resumed just 15 days after the June ceasefire agreement, arguing that Tehran would not accept an arrangement simply to escape the current situation.

A step back: On Trump’s no-war, no-deal approach against Iran

On the nuclear issue, the Iranian Foreign Minister said Tehran was open to negotiations over its stockpile of uranium enriched to 60% but ruled out transferring the material outside the country. He maintained that a fair formula could be reached on uranium enrichment, provided it formed part of a broader agreement addressing Iran's national interests and security concerns.

Mr. Araghchi also confirmed that Tehran and Washington continued exchanging messages and proposals through mediators, including Qatar and Pakistan. "We are people of diplomacy, and we still have hope in diplomacy," he said.

Meanwhile, he maintained that Iran remained willing to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if Washington fulfilled its conditions, underlining Tehran's position that any diplomatic settlement must address its nuclear programme, sanctions and security concerns.

articles.title: Russia dusts off its pre-war demands as the U.S. raises discussing European security at Ukraine talks
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The proposal to discuss broader security arrangements for Europe was floated by Donald Trump’s envoys, and that has worried Ukraine and its Western allies, who fear it will play into Moscow’s hands and weaken NATO

After nearly five years of fighting in Ukraine, the Kremlin is eagerly embracing a U.S. offer to discuss post-war European security, and Moscow is using that diplomatic opening to reaffirm the tough demands that President Vladimir Putin put forward before the start of his full-scale invasion.

The proposal to discuss broader security arrangements for Europe was floated by U.S. President Donald Trump 's envoys, and that has worried Ukraine and its Western allies, who fear it will play into Moscow's hands and weaken NATO.
The Kremlin strongly backed the U.S. idea, describing a review of the broader European security framework as vital for a settlement of Europe's most devastating conflict since World War II.

Mr. Putin discussed the Ukrainian conflict with Mr. Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, their first trilateral meeting . That encounter had fuelled fears in Ukraine that they could discuss a possible settlement without Kyiv's participation.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wants a ceasefire to include a security framework to ensure that Russia does not attack his country again, and European leaders argue that such an architecture already exists in the form of NATO.

In draft agreements submitted to the U.S. and NATO in December 2021, two months before the invasion, Russia demanded that Washington and its allies pledge to exclude NATO's expansion to Ukraine, Georgia or any other nation that was once part of the Soviet Union.
Moscow also demanded that the U.S. and its allies make a commitment to not deploy weapons or conduct any military activities in Ukraine and other ex-Soviet nations.
The documents also obliged the alliance not to station any troops in areas where they weren't present in 1997 — before NATO moved to incorporate former Soviet bloc countries and ex-Soviet republics.

They also suggested a freeze on patrols by Russian and U.S. warships and bombers near each other's borders. In addition, they called for efforts to reduce the risk of incidents involving Russia and NATO warships and aircraft, primarily in the Baltic and the Black seas; a reduction in the scope of military drills; and greater transparency and other confidence-building measures.
NATO allies have rejected the Russian demands as a nonstarter.
